title: Recognize bound Drizzle SQL execution without hiding raw SQL injection

Cite exact changed findings and retained negative denominator; no generic security-safety claim. Extend existing quality suite, manual edits and checksums; release/pin only after required checks. Linked consumer: communitai-hdja and9u4b. Keep open for unexecuted broad checks.

title: Epic A: Engine core — shared module library, contract v2, single-pass analysis
description:
## Background (reality check 2026-09-02, UBS v5.3.13)
The reality check compared README/AGENTS claims with the code and measured behaviour: 440/440 manifest cases pass, but single-file scans take 4.6–5.8 s (README says < 1 s), a 29K-line fixture tree takes 40 s (README: 3.2 s for 50K lines), a 124K-line Python project takes 143 s, and a 407K-line TypeScript tree hits the 300 s module timeout with 840 MB RSS. The project fails its own gate (`./ubs . --ci` → 9 critical findings, all false positives of the Python constant-time-compare detector). Ten modules are copy-pasted siblings with drifted primitives, five documented meta-runner flags do not exist, inline suppression and severity normalisation are implemented in one module each, helper checksum mismatches fail open during scans, the installer aborts on a clean first install, the Claude Code save hook is never registered, and the docs (AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, modules/README.md, README) drift from the code.

## Goal
Replace ten copy-pasted Bash modules with ten thin producers on top of one shared library (modules/lib/ubs-common.sh) and one stdlib-only Python analysis package (modules/helpers/ubs_core/). Every module then satisfies the same contract (modules/contract.json): identical flags, identical output formats rendered by one renderer, identical suppression semantics (implemented once, at count time), one severity vocabulary, language-prefixed stable category and rule ids, and a fixed process budget (≤ 25 processes per module run instead of hundreds).

## Why this is first
Fixes currently land in one language and never propagate (GH #85 two-tier constant-time vocabulary → Rust only; GH #91 suppression placement → JS only). Measured: the JS module on 407 TypeScript files ran 900 s at ~18% CPU, i.e. the run is dominated by fork/exec and pipe serialisation of per-category `rg | grep | awk | wc | python3` pipelines, not by analysis. The performance (C), parity (D), and new-language (I) workstreams all become cheap once this lands, and impossible to do ten times otherwise.

## Findings record (produced by every module, rendered by one renderer)
{"schema":"ubs.finding/1","lang":"python","rule_id":"py.security.ct-compare","category_id":"python.security","severity":"critical","confidence":0.82,"file":"src/auth.py","line":42,"col":9,"end_line":42,"end_col":31,"message":"Secret compared with ==","remediation":"Use hmac.compare_digest()","fix":{"kind":"replace","range":[42,9,42,31],"text":"hmac.compare_digest(a, b)"},"fingerprint":"sha256:…","suppressed":false,"source":"ast|regex|helper","extras":{}}
fingerprint = sha256(rule_id ‖ relative path ‖ whitespace-and-identifier-normalised statement text ‖ ordinal among identical statements) so it survives line shifts and local renames; emitted as SARIF partialFingerprints.ubs/v1.

## Contract v2 summary
Flags: --format=text|json|jsonl|sarif|toon, --ci, --fail-on-warning, -v, -q, --jobs=N, --files-from=PATH (NUL-separated), --exclude=GLOBS, --exclude-tests, --strict-gitignore, --category=CSV, --skip=CSV, --rules=DIR, --emit-findings-json=PATH, --list-rules, --dump-rules=DIR, --list-categories, --include-ext=CSV, OUTPUT_FILE positional. Exit 0 clean / 1 findings per policy / 2 environment or usage; --list-*/--dump-rules never scan and exit 0. Env: UBS_PROFILE, UBS_CATEGORY_FILTER, UBS_SKIP_TYPE_NARROWING (value 1 only), UBS_VERIFIED_ASSET_DIR, NO_COLOR; LC_ALL=C exported to child tools. Summary keys: language, files, critical, warning, info, categories[], findings[], extras{profile}. Category ids <lang>.<slug>; rule ids <lang>.<area>.<slug>, stable (renames via a rule_aliases table).

## Done when
contract_conformance.py is green for all ten modules, manifest totals are unchanged per ported module (golden-diffed), ubs-java.sh is under 4,000 lines, and UBS_PROFILE reports ≤ 25 processes per module run.


## Acceptance Criteria
All child beads closed with their acceptance tests green in CI; the epic's 'Done when' statement verified by a fresh scan and documented in CHANGELOG.

## Testing and logging requirements (apply to every bead)
- Unit tests live under test-suite/quality/ (Python, unittest, run by test-suite/run_all.sh) or test-suite/shareable/ for meta-runner behaviour; installer tests under test-suite/install/run_tests.sh. Every test prints a `[case-id] RUN/PASS/FAIL (elapsed)` line and, on failure, the full stdout/stderr it captured, so a swarm agent can diagnose from the log alone.
- E2E scripts must run the real `./ubs` (or the real module) against real fixture files with `--ci --format=json`, assert on exact rule ids / counts, and write artifacts under test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/ (stdout.log, stderr.log, result.json).
- Any change to modules/ubs-*.sh or modules/helpers/* must be followed by `./scripts/update_checksums.sh` and `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`; the CI drift check will flag modules against the last tag until the next release is cut (see the cut-release bead).
- Run `shellcheck -S warning` on touched shell files and `./ubs <touched files> --ci` before closing.

## Success Criteria
Ten modules pass contract_conformance.py; each module run spawns ≤ 25 processes; manifest totals unchanged per port; ubs-java.sh < 4,000 lines.
close_reason: Completed Epic A: All 20 child subtasks completed. All 10 language modules are now ported to contract v2 on ubs-common.sh + ubs_core, 100% PASS on contract conformance harness with UNPORTED_ALLOWLIST emptied, 472/472 manifest test cases pass, shellcheck -S warning clean, ~65,000 lines of legacy code removed, and documented in CHANGELOG.md.

title: A1: Create modules/lib/ubs-common.sh (argv parser, locale, file listing, suppression-aware counting, renderer)
description:
## What
Create modules/lib/ubs-common.sh, sourced by every module, providing the primitives that today exist in 4–7 drifted copies:
- `ubs_parse_args` implementing the contract-v2 flag set (see epic A), rejecting unknown flags with exit 2 and validating --format against text|json|jsonl|sarif|toon (today 8/10 modules silently fall back to text for toon/jsonl: ubs-js.sh:308, ubs-python.sh:318, ubs-golang.sh:258, ubs-rust.sh:214, ubs-cpp.sh:176, ubs-java.sh:236, ubs-ruby.sh:214, ubs-elixir.sh:187).
- Locale: `export LC_ALL=C` for child tools (7 modules assign LC_ALL=C without exporting: ubs-js.sh:331, ubs-golang.sh:314, ubs-rust.sh:508, ubs-cpp.sh:263, ubs-java.sh:335, ubs-ruby.sh:405, ubs-elixir.sh:2103, so `sort`/`grep` inherit the user's locale), with a UTF-8 override only for Python helpers that need it.
- `ubs_list_files`: one NUL-separated file list per module run (rg --files with the ignore globs, `-xdev`, honouring --files-from from the meta-runner, --include-ext, --exclude, --exclude-tests, --strict-gitignore), vendor-layout aware (node_modules/.bun, .pnpm, symlinked packages). Replaces seven file-count implementations of which only three are NUL-safe.
- `count_lines` that is suppression-aware at count time (delegating to the interval index from A7 once available; same-line + previous-line fallback until then).
- `json_escape` (one body; today five bodies with `${1:-}`/`${1-}`/`""`/`"$1"` drift — the swift/csharp forms break under set -u), `normalize_severity` (today only ubs-swift.sh:93), `with_timeout`, `die`.
- `finding_emit` writing findings records (schema ubs.finding/1) to a per-run NDJSON sink, and one renderer producing text/json/jsonl/sarif/toon from that sink (toon via the `tru` shim, exit 2 if missing).

## Why
Every later fix (suppression, severity, formats, locale, NUL safety) must land once. The library is checksum-verified and distributed exactly like helpers (A6).

## Acceptance Criteria
- quality/test_ubs_common.py exercises parser (unknown flag → 2, bad format → 2, every contract flag accepted), json_escape on control characters/quotes/unicode, normalize_severity table, NUL-safe listing with newline-containing paths, renderer output validity (json parses, sarif validates, jsonl one object per line, toon via tru).
- shellcheck -S warning clean on the library.
- Library listed in HELPER_ASSETS/HELPER_CHECKSUMS (A6).

Every test prints a `[case-id] RUN/PASS/FAIL (elapsed)` line and, on failure, the full stdout/stderr it captured, so a swarm agent can diagnose from the log alone.
- E2E scripts must run the real `./ubs` (or the real module) against real fixture files with `--ci --format=json`, assert on exact rule ids / counts, and write artifacts under test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/ (stdout.log, stderr.log, result.json).
- Any change to modules/ubs-*.sh or modules/helpers/* must be followed by `./scripts/update_checksums.sh` and `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`; the CI drift check will flag modules against the last tag until the next release is cut (see the cut-release bead).
- Run `shellcheck -S warning` on touched shell files and `./ubs <touched files> --ci` before closing.

title: A3b: modules/contract.json — machine-readable module contract; modules/README.md Options block generated from it; docs-claims cross-checks both against the parsers
description:
## What

Per module: `extensions`, `manifest_files`, `contract` version (1 today; 2 after its A4 port). Generate the Options block of modules/README.md from contract.json (a small stdlib script, scripts/gen_module_readme.py, idempotent, `--check` mode) and extend scripts/check_docs_claims.py: (a) the README block equals the generated block, (b) every flag in contract.json exists in the parsers it is claimed for (reuse the existing module-readme check's arm scanner), (c) every parser flag that is in ≥ 7 modules is listed in contract.json (so drift in either direction is a red gate).

## Why
Bead A3's first half. The README was hand-corrected on 2026-09-02 and a checker now verifies its claims against the parsers, but there is still no machine-readable source that B4c (per-language file lists need `extensions`/`manifest_files`), A8 (contract_conformance runs every module through every contract flag) and the scaffold (A3c) can consume. contract.json is that source; the README is derived from it, so there is exactly one place to edit.

## How
1. Author contract.json by reading each module's argument parser and `--help` (do not trust the help text alone: swift's help omits flags its parser accepts; the static arm scan in check_docs_claims.py is the ground truth for existence).
2. scripts/gen_module_readme.py: renders the Options block (same wording as today's block so the diff is empty on first run) between markers `<!-- contract:options -->` … `<!-- /contract:options -->` in modules/README.md; `--check` exits 1 on drift (run_all docs-claims step calls it).
3. check_docs_claims.py: the three checks above; the planted-false-claim technique from the module-readme check documents how to prove it.
4. `ubs --schema=contract` (optional, cheap): print contract.json so agents can fetch it; add to robot-docs formats if done.

## Acceptance Criteria
- contract.json lists all 10 modules with extensions/manifest files; gen script idempotent; docs-claims green with the new checks; a planted mismatch (flag removed from a parser) fails the gate.

## Testing and logging requirements (apply to every bead)
- Unit tests live under test-suite/quality/ (Python, unittest, run by test-suite/run_all.sh) or test-suite/shareable/ for meta-runner behaviour; installer tests under test-suite/install/run_tests.sh. Every test prints a `[case-id] RUN/PASS/FAIL (elapsed)` line and, on failure, the full stdout/stderr it captured, so a swarm agent can diagnose from the log alone.
- E2E checks run the real `./ubs` (or the real module) against real fixture files with `--ci --format=json`, assert on exact rule ids / counts, and write artifacts under test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/.
- Any change to modules/ubs-*.sh, modules/helpers/* or modules/lib/* must be followed by `./scripts/update_checksums.sh` and `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`; any change to `ubs` or `install.sh` by `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`.
- Run `shellcheck -S warning` on touched shell files, `python3 scripts/check_docs_claims.py`, and `./ubs <touched files> --ci` before closing. Gates must run on a frozen tree with no other scans in flight (cargo's global lock and the module timeout checks are load-sensitive).
- Never close on a self-report: cite the gate output (run_all.sh, cli-contract, manifest case ids) in the closing comment, and name anything that could not be verified here (e.g. a CI job on a platform this box does not have).

description:
## What

Keep every existing helper filename as a 3-line entrypoint (`from ubs_core.analyzers import …; main()`) so HELPER_CHECKSUMS continuity and standalone use are preserved.

## Why
Today each category spawns its own python3 (and dozens of rg/grep/awk/wc processes). One interpreter per module run is the single biggest process-count reduction and the only way to share analyzers across languages.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `python3 -m ubs_core --self-test` runs embedded unit tests for every analyzer; existing helper unit tests (python/tests, java/tests, csharp/tests) pass unchanged.
- Manifest totals unchanged for every language after migration (golden diff reviewed).

title: A3c: scripts/new-module.sh <lang> — scaffold a contract-v2 module (sources ubs-common.sh, rule-pack dirs, fixtures, manifest entries) that A8 accepts for a dummy language
description:
## What
`scripts/new-module.sh <lang> --extensions a,b --display-name 'X'` writes modules/ubs-<lang>.sh (strict mode, the ubs-common.sh source block used by all modules since bead A1, the shared flag core from contract.json, `ubs_validate_format`, `ubs_list_files` file discovery, a text/json/sarif renderer skeleton with the summary keys from contract.json, one example ast-grep rule pack directory `modules/rules/<lang>/` if the language has a tree-sitter grammar in ast-grep, and a heuristic-only path otherwise), test-suite/<lang>/{buggy,clean}/ with one fixture pair and a README explaining what each fixture proves, two manifest.json cases (<lang>-buggy expecting ≥1 critical, <lang>-clean expecting 0), and appends the module to ALL_LANGS/MODULE_CHECKSUMS scaffolding instructions (printed, not applied — the checksum scripts do that). Refuses to overwrite existing files (RULE 1).

## Why
Bead A3's second half and the prerequisite for I1 (Bash module) and I2 (Kotlin split): a module skeleton that starts on contract v2 means the A4 ports do not grow a new legacy module in parallel. A8 (0xjg.17, contract_conformance.py) is the judge: the scaffold's output for a dummy language must pass every contract flag/format check.

## How
1. Template as a heredoc inside new-module.sh (no new template directory); fill from contract.json (A3b) so the flag list cannot drift.
2. Dry run: `scripts/new-module.sh zig --extensions zig --dry-run` prints the file list; real run creates them; `bash -n` + shellcheck -S error on the result; the scaffolded module scans its own clean fixture with 0 findings and its buggy fixture with ≥ 1 (the template ships one trivial heuristic rule, e.g. a TODO/FIXME info finding plus one `eval`-style critical pattern the fixture pair exercises).
3. Quality test test-suite/quality/test_new_module.py: scaffold into a temp copy of the repo layout, run the generated module on its fixtures, run contract_conformance.py if A8 exists (skip with a message otherwise), assert nothing outside the expected paths was written.
4. AGENTS.md/modules/README.md: "Adding a module" section pointing at the script; CHANGELOG.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Generated dummy module passes bash -n, shellcheck -S error, its two manifest cases and (when A8 lands) contract_conformance; test_new_module green; no existing file is ever overwritten.

## Testing and logging requirements (apply to every bead)

- E2E checks run the real `./ubs` (or the real module) against real fixture files with `--ci --format=json`, assert on exact rule ids / counts, and write artifacts under test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/.
- Any change to modules/ubs-*.sh, modules/helpers/* or modules/lib/* must be followed by `./scripts/update_checksums.sh` and `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`; any change to `ubs` or `install.sh` by `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`.

title: Epic D: Detector parity and calibration — registry, shared analyzers, FP corpus, confidence
description:
## Background (reality check 2026-09-02, UBS v5.3.13)
The reality check compared README/AGENTS claims with the code and measured behaviour: 440/440 manifest cases pass, but single-file scans take 4.6–5.8 s (README says < 1 s), a 29K-line fixture tree takes 40 s (README: 3.2 s for 50K lines), a 124K-line Python project takes 143 s, and a 407K-line TypeScript tree hits the 300 s module timeout with 840 MB RSS. The project fails its own gate (`./ubs . --ci` → 9 critical findings, all false positives of the Python constant-time-compare detector). Ten modules are copy-pasted siblings with drifted primitives, five documented meta-runner flags do not exist, inline suppression and severity normalisation are implemented in one module each, helper checksum mismatches fail open during scans, the installer aborts on a clean first install, the Claude Code save hook is never registered, and the docs (AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, modules/README.md, README) drift from the code.

## Goal
Every detector family that exists in one language exists in every language where the concept applies, driven by a machine-readable registry (detectors.yml) from which the README coverage matrix is generated and against which the harness asserts fixture pairs. Findings carry a calibrated `confidence`, and the README's false-positive claim (8–12%) is replaced by a measured, nightly-enforced number.

## Evidence of the gap
Constant-time-compare detector exists in 4/10 modules and only Rust has the GH #85 two-tier vocabulary; Python (ubs-python.sh:4315) and Go (ubs-golang.sh:6103) use a flat substring regex that flags `TARGET_SIGS.get(sig) == "asyncio_task"` and `if token == "rm":` as CRITICAL — these are the 9 self-scan false positives. deep_guard exists in 3/10 (js, python, ruby). Type narrowing in 5/10. ast-grep rule packs: rust 77, go 64, python 52, js 37, java 34, cpp 32, ruby 28, csharp 4, swift 1, elixir 0. Taint exists in all 10 but swift/elixir have no provenance path and no module resets taint state at function boundaries. normalize_severity() exists in 1/10 (swift).

## Mechanisms
Registry + generated matrix; shared analyzers in ubs_core (epic A); a monotone-framework taint engine with function summaries (Kildall worklist, Sharir–Pnueli functional summaries) replacing per-language loops; FP corpus of pinned clean OSS repos with stratified (Neyman) sampling; split-conformal per-detector confidence with a marginal coverage guarantee; SPRT-gated nightly budgets; submodular (greedy, ≥ 1−1/e) selection of smoke fixtures per CPU second.


## Acceptance Criteria
All child beads closed with their acceptance tests green in CI; the epic's 'Done when' statement verified by a fresh scan and documented in CHANGELOG.

## Testing and logging requirements (apply to every bead)
- Unit tests live under test-suite/quality/ (Python, unittest, run by test-suite/run_all.sh) or test-suite/shareable/ for meta-runner behaviour; installer tests under test-suite/install/run_tests.sh. Every test prints a `[case-id] RUN/PASS/FAIL (elapsed)` line and, on failure, the full stdout/stderr it captured, so a swarm agent can diagnose from the log alone.
- E2E scripts must run the real `./ubs` (or the real module) against real fixture files with `--ci --format=json`, assert on exact rule ids / counts, and write artifacts under test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/ (stdout.log, stderr.log, result.json).
- Any change to modules/ubs-*.sh or modules/helpers/* must be followed by `./scripts/update_checksums.sh` and `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`; the CI drift check will flag modules against the last tag until the next release is cut (see the cut-release bead).

## Success Criteria
detectors.yml has no unexplained gaps; `./ubs . --ci --fail-on-warning` exits 0 on this repo; nightly FP corpus within budget; findings carry calibrated confidence.

title: D10: Rust cargo phases — a tool failure without diagnostics (rch exit 103, 'remote build admission is paused', missing toolchain) is a warning + 'not evaluated' with status partial, never a critical; the wrapper's message is surfaced verbatim
description:
## What
Since the cargo phases started running for real (fix for "cargo phases ran nothing from v5.0.0 to v5.3.13", 2026-09-02), a cargo invocation that fails without producing rustc diagnostics is reported by modules/ubs-rust.sh as a CRITICAL per phase ("cargo check failed without diagnostics (exit 103)", "cargo test --no-run failed without diagnostics (exit 1)") plus a warning for clippy. On this development box cargo is shimmed through rch (remote build offload); when the fleet is degraded it returns exit 103 "[RCH] remote required; refusing local fallback" or exit 1 "remote build admission is paused while daemon restart remediation is active". Result: three false criticals on a clean crate, the rust-clean manifest case red for a day, and anyone running UBS behind a build wrapper or on a host without a working toolchain gets a red scan for reasons unrelated to their code. Reclassify: cargo could not run (non-zero exit, no `error[` / `error:` rustc diagnostics in the log) → one WARNING "cargo <phase> could not run (exit N)" carrying the wrapper's first stderr lines, a "Not evaluated" info line for the phase (the same shape --no-cargo produces since #99), and module `status: partial` with `module_error: CARGO_UNAVAILABLE` in the summary JSON so the meta-runner's envelope reports `status: partial` (exit 2 unless UBS_ALLOW_PARTIAL=1) instead of exit 1 with criticals. Real diagnostics (rustc errors, clippy lints, test build failures with messages) stay critical/warning exactly as today.

## Why
Severity must reflect the code, not the toolchain: a critical means "your code has a problem"; "I could not run cargo" is an environment condition that the error envelope (bead B6) already knows how to express as partial. The other agent who wrote report_cargo_failure chose critical for check/test; this bead is the calibration follow-up and should be discussed with them in the closing comment (their commit b7822ff, 2026-09-02).

## How
1. ubs-rust.sh report_cargo_failure: classify `no diagnostics` (the existing "without diagnostics" branch) → warning + not-evaluated + set `MODULE_STATUS=partial`, `MODULE_ERROR=CARGO_UNAVAILABLE`, include up to 3 stderr lines in the finding message (already captured in the log file); keep the diagnostics branch unchanged.
2. Summary JSON: `status` and `module_error` fields (contract.json documents them; the meta-runner already consumes `status`).
3. Manifest: rust-clean keeps `exit_code: zero` and `critical max 0`; add `rust-clean-cargo-unavailable` with env `PATH` pointing at a shim dir whose `cargo` exits 103 with the rch message → expect exit 2, status partial, 0 critical, the warning text, and `module_error: CARGO_UNAVAILABLE` (assert via findings_json_valid/require_substrings as the manifest supports).
4. README (Rust section) + robot-docs exit codes: "cargo unavailable → partial (exit 2)".

## Acceptance Criteria
- The new manifest case green; rust-clean green when cargo works (verify on a healthy rch posture or with UBS_SKIP_RUST_BUILD=1 for the static part); checksums regenerated; CHANGELOG entry.

## Testing and logging requirements (apply to every bead)
- Unit tests live under test-suite/quality/ (Python, unittest, run by test-suite/run_all.sh) or test-suite/shareable/ for meta-runner behaviour; installer tests under test-suite/install/run_tests.sh. Every test prints a `[case-id] RUN/PASS/FAIL (elapsed)` line and, on failure, the full stdout/stderr it captured, so a swarm agent can diagnose from the log alone.
- E2E checks run the real `./ubs` (or the real module) against real fixture files with `--ci --format=json`, assert on exact rule ids / counts, and write artifacts under test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/.
- Any change to modules/ubs-*.sh, modules/helpers/* or modules/lib/* must be followed by `./scripts/update_checksums.sh` and `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`; any change to `ubs` or `install.sh` by `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`.
- Run `shellcheck -S warning` on touched shell files, `python3 scripts/check_docs_claims.py`, and `./ubs <touched files> --ci` before closing. Gates must run on a frozen tree with no other scans in flight (cargo's global lock and the module timeout checks are load-sensitive).
- Never close on a self-report: cite the gate output (run_all.sh, cli-contract, manifest case ids) in the closing comment, and name anything that could not be verified here (e.g. a CI job on a platform this box does not have).

title: D7: Held-out detector accuracy, valid confidence and SPRT-gated budgets
description:
## Problem and objective
Finish the existing false-positive/accuracy program; do not create a second calibration framework. README currently claims layer FP rates of 15–20%, 2–5%, 1–3% and blended 8–12%, while explain.py defaults many rule records to high confidence and prints "(calibrated)" without matching empirical evidence. This is unproven, not measured precision. Existing strong frontends' semantic tests should be transferred to weaker modules, but fixture pass rates and warning tolerances do not calibrate those claims.

## Corpus and independent labels
Maintain pinned-commit, licensed OSS samples stratified by registered language, detector family and source-size bucket; fetch into allowed external cache/scratch locations without vendoring. Use pilot variance and explicit inclusion weights before claiming Neyman allocation. Preserve the requested per-detector FP confidence-interval half-width goal of at most three percentage points; publish actual intervals and sample requirements where that goal is not yet met rather than treating a small sample as proof. Annotate findings and sampled missed-bug/clean controls with independently reviewed per-rule ground truth. A directory called clean is not globally bug-free: current Go security fixtures omit resource cleanup, Rust clean cases allow six warnings, and Ruby's actually joined threads collection produces a lifecycle false positive. Record uncertain labels and inter-review disagreements rather than forcing them into true/false classes. Split by repository and code origin so related fixtures or donor mutations cannot leak across development/calibration/held-out evaluation.

## Statistically valid output
Publish per-language/per-detector held-out precision, recall where labels permit it, sample counts, intervals, corpus/source/tool/policy identity and drift caveats. Detectors with fewer than 50 independent calibration points, uncalibrated scores or distribution shift emit unknown/null confidence, and explain text must distinguish heuristic strength from calibrated evidence. Preserve the min-confidence feature goal only for a documented valid score semantics.
The old description incorrectly inferred that split-conformal marginal coverage implies findings above confidence c are true positives with probability at least c. It does not. If conformal prediction is used, define the prediction-set/nonconformity construction, calibration split, exchangeability assumptions, finite-sample marginal coverage target and empirical held-out coverage; do not advertise per-finding or thresholded precision as the same guarantee. A calibrated TP score/threshold precision claim requires its own independent validity and uncertainty evidence. Primary background: https://arxiv.org/html/2107.07511v6.

## Nightly gate and drift
Retain sequential regression detection, explicit FP budgets, H0: FP rate at most budget versus H1: at least budget plus a documented delta, and alpha=beta=0.05 goals. Specify the sampling/independence assumptions under which SPRT applies; avoid optional-stopping claims from a one-off fixed interval. Test type-I/type-II behavior on independently generated stable and changed distributions. Record persistent drift without refreshing goldens/budgets to make it green. Respect old accuracy/performance gates or meet the legitimate gate-fix standard if a real gate defect is proven. README tables come from valid versioned measurements through J1, not invented probabilities.

## Implementation and acceptance
Extend existing detector/registry/explain/output and nightly/harness integration. Every activated or ported family needs independent unsafe/safe controls and actual ordinary-CLI JSON/SARIF tests with exact public IDs and selected scope; transferred donor tests must match receiver semantics. Use the named calibration-probe authoring task for independent statistical and output oracles, then cite its fixed-behavior green artifacts before closure. Test null/unknown confidence, sparse samples, repo split/leakage, label weights, drift, supported score filtering and unchanged default scan semantics.
Required module/helper checksums, version/release handling and prescribed checks apply after future implementation; no implementation completed by this audit. Write all test artifacts under test-suite/artifacts/ with case/command/source/tool/run identities, elapsed time, exit and complete stdout/stderr. Honor the no-deletion rule and current owner reservations. Never close on a self-report, synthetic calibration tests alone, percentages from fixture counts, plan edits, or a mere nightly workflow file.


## Named independent probe
ultimate_bug_scanner-mj1j.41 authors the statistical/ordinary-CLI oracle first; D7 closure requires its final green artifacts, a real held-out corpus and observed nightly evidence. Probe-authoring expected-red closure alone is not calibration implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Named probe ultimate_bug_scanner-mj1j.41 is independently authored; final fixed-behavior/statistical CLI cases are green with cited artifacts.
- [ ] Pinned, licensed stratified corpus and independent origin-separated TP/FP/missed-bug labels publish weighted held-out precision/recall, actual intervals/counts and progress toward <=3 percentage-point interval half-width.
- [ ] Under 50 independent points, uncalibrated or shifted scores report null/unknown; JSON/SARIF/explain/min-confidence match documented valid semantics.
- [ ] Any conformal construction states exchangeability and marginal coverage; no thresholded-precision or per-finding probability claim follows from marginal coverage alone.
- [ ] SPRT retains explicit budgets/H0/H1/delta and alpha=beta=0.05 goals, independent type-I/II simulations and documented sampling assumptions; nightly current-corpus integration passes.
- [ ] README generated empirical tables replace unsupported percentages; synthetic tests alone do not establish detector accuracy. Prescribed checks, integrity and version/release rules pass for future code.
notes: Final refinement, October 6: explicitly define every accuracy/budget denominator. False-discovery proportion among reviewed findings (FP/(TP+FP)) differs from false-positive rate among independently labeled negative opportunities (FP/(FP+TN)); neither is recall. State the sampling unit, inclusion weights and repository clustering, obtain independently labeled negative opportunities before estimating the latter, and keep corpus/report/nightly gate denominators consistent. Missing ground truth cannot become zero false positives. Preserve the <=3 percentage-point interval half-width goal and alpha=beta=0.05 SPRT targets under documented valid assumptions; publish insufficient-evidence states.

comments.author: SwiftPine
comments.text:
October 6 mathematical/coverage refinement: preserve the 100% relevant-rule smoke target and deterministic measured-cost selection. First define the inventory as actual effective public rules, including counted/advisory/gated scope rather than raw AST-pattern rows. Ordinary cost-ratio greedy under a knapsack budget does not automatically inherit the cardinality 1-1/e approximation claim; either implement an algorithm with the claimed bound under its actual assumptions or report the measured heuristic without that guarantee. If 100% coverage is infeasible under the stated budget, publish the uncovered rules, feasible lower bound/witness and a named scope/budget blocker; do not silently relax coverage or call it done. This is a plan correctness correction, not a performance win or completed coverage. Independent ratio-greedy counterexample: budget 1; fixture A costs 1 and covers 1000 rules; fixture B costs 0.0009 and covers one of A's rules. Marginal-rules-per-cost selects B first (1111 > 1000), then A no longer fits, achieving 1/1000 of optimal unless additional algorithmic safeguards are implemented. Keep this as a mathematical unit oracle with the actual intended algorithm, not a test mirroring its implementation.

title: Fix script_dir() for Homebrew symlink resolution (GH#21)
description:
## Problem

`script_dir()` in `ubs:699` fails when UBS is invoked via Homebrew symlink because macOS `readlink` returns relative paths. The current implementation:

```bash
script_dir(){ local src="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"; while [ -h "$src" ]; do src="$(readlink "$src")"; done; cd -P "$(dirname "$src")" && pwd; }
```

When `readlink` returns a relative path (e.g., `../../Cellar/ubs/1.0/bin/ubs`), the next loop iteration tries to resolve this relative to CWD instead of relative to the symlink's parent directory.

## Root Cause

macOS `readlink` (BSD variant) returns the literal symlink target without canonicalizing. GNU `readlink` on Linux returns an absolute path. The portable fix is to `cd` into the symlink's parent directory before calling `readlink`, so relative paths resolve correctly.

## Implementation Plan

### Fix script_dir() (ubs:699)

Replace the one-liner with the portable pattern:

```bash
script_dir(){
    local src="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
    while [ -h "$src" ]; do
        local dir="$(cd -P "$(dirname "$src")" && pwd)"
        src="$(readlink "$src")"
        # If readlink returned a relative path, resolve against symlink's parent
        [[ "$src" != /* ]] && src="$dir/$src"
    done
    cd -P "$(dirname "$src")" && pwd
}
```

Key change: After `readlink`, check if the result is relative (doesn't start with `/`). If so, prepend the symlink's parent directory. This handles chains of relative symlinks correctly.

## Files to Modify

- `ubs` line 699 (script_dir function -- single line to multi-line)

## Usage sites that benefit

- `resolve_module_path()` at ubs:1646-1657 uses `script_dir` to find `modules/ubs-*.sh`
- Git detection at ubs:1860-1866 uses `script_dir` to check for `.git` directory
- Both break when script_dir returns wrong path via Homebrew symlink
acceptance_criteria:
1. `script_dir()` returns correct directory when invoked via Homebrew symlink on macOS
2. `script_dir()` still works when invoked directly (no symlink)
3. `script_dir()` works with chains of relative symlinks (A -> B -> C)
4. `script_dir()` works on Linux (GNU readlink, absolute paths)
5. Module resolution via `resolve_module_path()` finds modules correctly via symlink
6. No bash version requirement change (must work with bash 3.2+ on macOS)
notes:
## E2E Test Script (scripts/test_symlink_resolution.sh)

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
echo "=== script_dir() symlink resolution test ==="
PASS=0; FAIL=0

TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
REAL_DIR="$TMPDIR/real/bin"
LINK_DIR="$TMPDIR/links"
mkdir -p "$REAL_DIR" "$LINK_DIR"

# Create a minimal test script that sources script_dir and prints result
cat > "$REAL_DIR/test_script.sh" << 'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
script_dir(){
    local src="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
    while [ -h "$src" ]; do
        local dir="$(cd -P "$(dirname "$src")" && pwd)"
        src="$(readlink "$src")"
        [[ "$src" != /* ]] && src="$dir/$src"
    done
    cd -P "$(dirname "$src")" && pwd
}
echo "$(script_dir)"
SH
chmod +x "$REAL_DIR/test_script.sh"

# Test 1: Direct invocation
RESULT=$("$REAL_DIR/test_script.sh")
[[ "$RESULT" == "$REAL_DIR" ]] && ((PASS++)) || { echo "FAIL: direct invocation got '$RESULT' want '$REAL_DIR'"; ((FAIL++)); }

# Test 2: Single relative symlink
ln -sf "../../real/bin/test_script.sh" "$LINK_DIR/test_link"
RESULT=$("$LINK_DIR/test_link")
[[ "$RESULT" == "$REAL_DIR" ]] && ((PASS++)) || { echo "FAIL: relative symlink got '$RESULT' want '$REAL_DIR'"; ((FAIL++)); }

# Test 3: Absolute symlink
ln -sf "$REAL_DIR/test_script.sh" "$LINK_DIR/test_abs_link"
RESULT=$("$LINK_DIR/test_abs_link")
[[ "$RESULT" == "$REAL_DIR" ]] && ((PASS++)) || { echo "FAIL: absolute symlink got '$RESULT' want '$REAL_DIR'"; ((FAIL++)); }

# Test 4: Chain of symlinks
ln -sf "$LINK_DIR/test_link" "$LINK_DIR/test_chain"
RESULT=$("$LINK_DIR/test_chain")
[[ "$RESULT" == "$REAL_DIR" ]] && ((PASS++)) || { echo "FAIL: chain symlink got '$RESULT' want '$REAL_DIR'"; ((FAIL++)); }

echo "Results: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
[[ $FAIL -eq 0 ]] && echo "ALL PASS" || exit 1
```

title: Fix targeted scans bypassing explicit file/diff workflows
description:
Targeted UBS modes regress in large repos because the meta-runner performs whole-tree size checks and ignore-copy staging before narrowing to --diff/--staged/explicit files.

Symptoms:
- `ubs --diff` can fail with directory-too-large in big repos even when only a handful of files changed.
- `ubs file1 file2` / `ubs --files=...` hit full-repo staging first instead of respecting the target list.
- `ubs --version` also emits size-check diagnostics before the version string.

Goal:
- Make `--diff`, `--staged`, and explicit file scans avoid whole-tree size checks/copies.
- Make `--version` exit before unrelated scan guards.
- Add regression coverage.

title: Update all dependencies to latest stable versions
description:
## Dependency Update for ultimate_bug_scanner

### Context
UBS is a Bash script that manages external tool dependencies via uv (Python tools), npm, and system packages. "Updating dependencies" means ensuring all scanner tools are at latest versions.

### Steps
1. `cd /data/projects/ultimate_bug_scanner`
2. Check uv-managed Python tools: `uv tool list` -- note versions of bandit, semgrep, ruff, mypy, pylint
3. Update Python tools: `uv tool upgrade --all`
4. Check npm-managed tools: eslint, prettier versions in package.json if applicable
5. Run `./ubs --doctor` -- verify all scanners detected and working
6. Run `./ubs --python /data/projects/mcp_agent_mail` -- smoke test Python scanning
7. Verify module loading: each `modules/ubs-*.sh` should load without errors

### Key Tools to Watch
- `bandit` -- Python security scanner, new rules may change findings
- `semgrep` -- multi-language scanner, rule updates
- `ruff` -- Python linter (very fast iteration), new rules frequently
- `shellcheck` -- Bash linter
- `toon` -- TOON output formatter (custom tool)

### Verification
- `./ubs --doctor` passes all checks
- Python module runs without errors
- Bash module runs without errors
- Finding counts are reasonable (not zero, not explosion of new findings)

title: Feature: Publish toon_rust as library crate to crates.io
description:
## Overview

Publish toon_rust to crates.io as a library crate with both lib and bin targets, enabling Rust projects to use TOON encoding/decoding without spawning a subprocess.

## Background

Currently toon_rust is only available as a binary (`tru`). This works for CLI tools and bash scripts, but Rust projects that want TOON support must:
1. Shell out to the binary (subprocess overhead)
2. Parse stdout/stderr (fragile)
3. Handle binary availability (may not be installed)

A library crate solves all these issues.

## Proposed API

```rust
// lib.rs
pub fn encode(json: &str) -> Result<String, ToonError>;
pub fn encode_value(value: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<String, ToonError>;
pub fn decode(toon: &str) -> Result<String, ToonError>;
pub fn decode_value(toon: &str) -> Result<serde_json::Value, ToonError>;

// With options
pub fn encode_with_options(json: &str, opts: EncodeOptions) -> Result<String, ToonError>;

pub struct EncodeOptions {
    pub delimiter: Delimiter,      // Comma, Tab, Pipe
    pub indent: usize,             // Default 2
    pub key_folding: KeyFolding,   // Off, Safe
    pub flatten_depth: Option<usize>,
}
```

## Cargo.toml Structure

```toml
[package]
name = "toon"
version = "0.2.0"

[lib]
name = "toon"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "tru"
path = "src/main.rs"
```

## Usage Examples

```rust
use toon::{encode, decode};

let json = r#"{"name": "test", "values": [1, 2, 3]}"#;
let toon_output = encode(json)?;
let roundtrip = decode(&toon_output)?;
assert_eq!(json, roundtrip);
```

## Benefits

1. **No subprocess overhead** - Direct function calls
2. **Type safety** - Rust error handling
3. **Composability** - Use in pipelines, iterators
4. **Testability** - Unit test TOON encoding in Rust projects
5. **Discoverability** - Found via crates.io search

## Migration Path

- Existing binary users: No change (bin target still works)
- New Rust projects: `cargo add toon` and use library API
- UBS: Could optionally include as dependency if rewritten in Rust

## Dependencies

None - can be done independently.

## Notes

This work happens in the toon_rust repository.
Consider whether to rename the crate from `toon_rust` to just `toon`.

title: Pass .ubsignore patterns to bandit via -x flag (GH#22)
description:
## Problem

Bandit ignores .ubsignore patterns because the patterns from GLOBAL_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS are not passed to the bandit invocation. This produces 10,879 false findings from test files and other excluded paths.

## Root Cause

In `modules/ubs-python.sh:2746-2754`, bandit is invoked with `-x "${_EXC:-}"` where `_EXC` is built only from the hardcoded `EXCLUDE_DIRS` array (line 369-370). The `EXTRA_EXCLUDES` from `--exclude=` flag (line 212) gets appended to `EXCLUDE_DIRS` at line 370, but `GLOBAL_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` (populated from .ubsignore by `load_ignore_patterns()` in `ubs:57-97`) is only passed to modules via the `--exclude=` argument at `ubs:2024`. The module argument parser at line 212 puts this into `EXTRA_EXCLUDES`, which does get added to `EXCLUDE_DIRS`.

**Wait** -- re-reading the code flow more carefully:
1. `ubs` main script loads .ubsignore into `GLOBAL_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` (ubs:57-97)
2. `ubs` passes `--exclude=$GLOBAL_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` to each module (ubs:2024)
3. Module parses `--exclude=*` into `EXTRA_EXCLUDES` (ubs-python.sh:212)
4. `EXTRA_EXCLUDES` gets appended to `EXCLUDE_DIRS` (ubs-python.sh:370)
5. Bandit uses `EXCLUDE_DIRS` to build `-x` argument (ubs-python.sh:2746-2754)

This chain SHOULD work. The bug may be more subtle:
- The patterns in .ubsignore might use glob syntax (`modules/helpers/*.go`) that bandit's `-x` flag doesn't understand (it expects directory paths, not globs)
- Or `apply_ignore_filters()` (ubs:1436-1484) creates a filtered workspace via rsync, but bandit is invoked against the original `PROJECT_DIR` instead of `FILTERED_PROJECT_DIR`

### Likely actual fix

The `apply_ignore_filters()` function at ubs:1436-1484 creates `FILTERED_PROJECT_DIR` and sets `PROJECT_DIR` to it. Bandit (and all other tools) should use this filtered dir. Verify that `PROJECT_DIR` is correctly set to the filtered copy BEFORE modules run. If the filtering fails (no rsync), the patterns need to be converted to bandit-compatible -x paths.

## Implementation Plan

### 1. Verify the filter chain (ubs main script)

Check that `apply_ignore_filters()` runs before module dispatch and that `PROJECT_DIR` is updated to `FILTERED_PROJECT_DIR`. If not, move the call earlier.

### 2. Convert glob patterns to directory paths for bandit

Bandit's `-x` flag expects comma-separated directory/file paths, not globs. Add a conversion step in ubs-python.sh before building the bandit command:

```bash
# Convert glob patterns to expanded paths
local -a bandit_excludes=()
for d in "${EXCLUDE_DIRS[@]}"; do
    # If it's a glob, expand it
    if [[ "$d" == *"*"* ]]; then
        while IFS= read -r match; do
            bandit_excludes+=("$match")
        done < <(find "$PROJECT_DIR" -path "$PROJECT_DIR/$d" 2>/dev/null)
    else
        bandit_excludes+=("$d")
    fi
done
```

### 3. Verify with test suite directory

The .ubsignore contains `test-suite/` which is the main source of false positives. After the fix, `bandit -q -r "$PROJECT_DIR" -x "test-suite"` should skip all files under test-suite/.

## Files to Modify

- `modules/ubs-python.sh` lines 2746-2754 (bandit invocation)
- `ubs` lines 1436-1484 (verify filter chain runs before modules)
- `.ubsignore` (verify patterns are bandit-compatible)
acceptance_criteria:
1. Running UBS on a project with .ubsignore correctly excludes listed paths from bandit scan
2. `test-suite/` in .ubsignore eliminates test file false positives from bandit output
3. Glob patterns in .ubsignore (e.g., `modules/helpers/*.go`) are correctly handled
4. Other scanners (semgrep, ruff, etc.) continue to work with .ubsignore patterns
5. The filtered workspace approach (rsync) works when rsync is available
6. Fallback to direct -x passing works when rsync is not available
7. Finding count drops significantly (from ~10,879 to expected real findings only)
notes:
## E2E Test

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
echo "=== UBS Bandit .ubsignore E2E Test ==="

# Setup: create temp project with test files
TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$TMPDIR/src" "$TMPDIR/test-suite"

# Real code (should be scanned)
cat > "$TMPDIR/src/app.py" << 'PY'
import subprocess
subprocess.call(input("cmd: "), shell=True)  # Should flag: B602
PY

# Test code (should be EXCLUDED)
cat > "$TMPDIR/test-suite/test_app.py" << 'PY'
import subprocess
subprocess.call("echo test", shell=True)  # Should NOT appear
PY

# Create .ubsignore
echo "test-suite/" > "$TMPDIR/.ubsignore"

# Run UBS
echo "[1/3] Running UBS without .ubsignore..."
BEFORE=$(cd "$TMPDIR" && ubs --python --no-ubsignore 2>&1 | grep -c "B602" || echo 0)
echo "  Bandit B602 findings: $BEFORE"

echo "[2/3] Running UBS with .ubsignore..."
AFTER=$(cd "$TMPDIR" && ubs --python 2>&1 | grep -c "B602" || echo 0)
echo "  Bandit B602 findings: $AFTER"

echo "[3/3] Verify reduction..."
if [[ "$AFTER" -lt "$BEFORE" ]]; then
    echo "PASS: .ubsignore reduced findings from $BEFORE to $AFTER"
else
    echo "FAIL: .ubsignore did not reduce bandit findings ($BEFORE -> $AFTER)"
    exit 1
fi
```

description:
## Overview

The UBS installer (`install.sh`) must automatically download and install the toon_rust `tru` binary as part of the standard installation process. Users should NOT need to manually:
- Download toon_rust
- Build from source
- Set TOON_TRU_BIN/TOON_BIN environment variable
- Configure shell profiles

Everything must be fully automated, just like ast-grep, ripgrep, and jq installations are today.

## Background & Rationale

### Current State
- UBS supports `--format=toon` for ~50% smaller output (optimized for LLM token efficiency)
- TOON encoding uses the toon_rust `tru` binary (Node.js toon CLI is not permitted)
- User must manually set `TOON_TRU_BIN=/path/to/tru` to force the fast Rust version
- This friction means most users miss the fast Rust encoder by default

### Why This Matters
- toon_rust is ~10x faster than the Node.js implementation
- No Node.js runtime dependency required
- Consistent with UBS philosophy: batteries-included, zero-config
- TOON format is critical for AI/LLM workflows where token efficiency matters

### Naming Conflict Issue
- Original toon_rust binary name conflicted with the Unix translate command
- Solution: use the `tru` binary name everywhere and install as `tru` in ~/.local/bin
- UBS already sets `TOON_TRU_BIN`, so the binary name is abstracted away

## Success Criteria
1. Fresh UBS install automatically downloads platform-appropriate toon_rust binary
2. Binary installed to ~/.local/bin/tru (or platform equivalent)
3. TOON_TRU_BIN automatically configured (shell profile or ubs internal default)
4. `ubs --format=toon` works out-of-box with Rust encoder
5. No Node.js fallback (only toon_rust)
6. Works on Linux (x86_64, arm64) and macOS (x86_64, arm64)

## Architecture Notes
- Follow existing patterns from install.sh (see ast-grep, ripgrep, jq downloads)
- Use GitHub releases for binary distribution
- Verify checksums for security
- Support --dry-run for testing

title: Core: Auto-configure TOON_BIN in ubs script
description:
## Task

Modify the ubs script to automatically detect and use the installed `tru` binary without requiring user configuration.

## Current State

```bash
# In ubs script (line ~147)
# TOON_BIN should default to tru (toon_rust); Node `toon` is forbidden
```

## Proposed Change

```bash
# Auto-detect toon_rust binary location (no Node.js fallback)
detect_toon_bin() {
  local candidates=(
    "$HOME/.local/bin/tru"     # Standard install location
    "$HOME/.cargo/bin/tru"     # Cargo install location
    "/usr/local/bin/tru"       # System-wide install
  )
  for bin in "${candidates[@]}"; do
    if [[ -x "$bin" ]]; then
      echo "$bin"
      return 0
    fi
  done
  # Fall back to PATH lookup
  if command -v tru >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v tru
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

# Resolution order: TOON_TRU_BIN > TOON_BIN > tru (PATH)
TOON_BIN="${TOON_TRU_BIN:-${TOON_BIN:-tru}}"
```

## Why This Approach

1. **Zero user configuration** - Works out of box after installation
2. **Respects user override** - TOON_TRU_BIN/TOON_BIN env var still works
3. **No Node.js fallback** - Only toon_rust encoder is accepted
4. **Multiple install locations** - Supports different installation methods

## Location

Modify ubs script near line 147 where TOON_BIN is defined.

## Dependencies

- ultimate_bug_scanner-3a6.4 (Core: integration - binary must be installed first)

## Testing

- Fresh install: should auto-detect ~/.local/bin/tru
- Manual override: TOON_TRU_BIN=/custom/path should work
- Missing tru: should warn and fall back to JSON output (no Node.js)

title: Epic I: Language coverage — Bash module (self-hosting), Kotlin split
description:
## Background (reality check 2026-09-02, UBS v5.3.13)
The reality check compared README/AGENTS claims with the code and measured behaviour: 440/440 manifest cases pass, but single-file scans take 4.6–5.8 s (README says < 1 s), a 29K-line fixture tree takes 40 s (README: 3.2 s for 50K lines), a 124K-line Python project takes 143 s, and a 407K-line TypeScript tree hits the 300 s module timeout with 840 MB RSS. The project fails its own gate (`./ubs . --ci` → 9 critical findings, all false positives of the Python constant-time-compare detector). Ten modules are copy-pasted siblings with drifted primitives, five documented meta-runner flags do not exist, inline suppression and severity normalisation are implemented in one module each, helper checksum mismatches fail open during scans, the installer aborts on a clean first install, the Claude Code save hook is never registered, and the docs (AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, modules/README.md, README) drift from the code.

## Goal
UBS is 77K lines of Bash and cannot scan itself (`ubs .` on a shell-only tree exits 3). Add a Bash module built with the epic-A scaffold so the project passes its own gate, seeded with fixture pairs for the real Bash bugs found in this audit (`((x++))` under set -e, `local x=$(cmd)` masking, `$?` after `if !`, unexported LC_ALL, unquoted expansions). Split Kotlin out of the Java module into a first-class module.


## Acceptance Criteria
All child beads closed with their acceptance tests green in CI; the epic's 'Done when' statement verified by a fresh scan and documented in CHANGELOG.

## Testing and logging requirements (apply to every bead)
- Unit tests live under test-suite/quality/ (Python, unittest, run by test-suite/run_all.sh) or test-suite/shareable/ for meta-runner behaviour; installer tests under test-suite/install/run_tests.sh. Every test prints a `[case-id] RUN/PASS/FAIL (elapsed)` line and, on failure, the full stdout/stderr it captured, so a swarm agent can diagnose from the log alone.
- E2E scripts must run the real `./ubs` (or the real module) against real fixture files with `--ci --format=json`, assert on exact rule ids / counts, and write artifacts under test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/ (stdout.log, stderr.log, result.json).
- Any change to modules/ubs-*.sh or modules/helpers/* must be followed by `./scripts/update_checksums.sh` and `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`; the CI drift check will flag modules against the last tag until the next release is cut (see the cut-release bead).
- Run `shellcheck -S warning` on touched shell files and `./ubs <touched files> --ci` before closing.

## Success Criteria
`ubs .` scans this repository's Bash and passes; Kotlin is a first-class language.
close_reason: Epic I completed: I1 (Bash module ubs-bash.sh with self-gate) and I2 (Kotlin split into first-class ubs-kotlin.sh module on contract v2) both implemented, fully tested, and passing

title: I1: modules/ubs-bash.sh — Bash/POSIX-sh module built with the scaffold; fixtures from this audit's real bugs; self-gate

title: K4: ubs serve / ubs --client — per-repo daemon answering incremental scans in < 100 ms
description:
## What
A per-repository daemon (`ubs serve`, Unix socket under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, idle auto-exit) that holds the language file lists, prefilter bitsets (C2), ast-grep --json=stream results and the Merkle cache (C4) warm; `ubs --client <file>` (or the agent hooks) sends changed paths and receives findings for just those files in < 100 ms; falls back to one-shot mode when no daemon is running; `ubs serve --watch` uses inotify/fsevents when available. This is the mechanism that turns "instant feedback" from a README claim into a property agents can rely on.

## Acceptance Criteria
- test_daemon.py: start daemon, warm, modify one file, client returns in < 100 ms with identical findings to a one-shot scan; daemon exits after idle timeout.

## Security note (added in refinement round 1)
The daemon socket must live under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (fallback: a 0700 directory under $XDG_CACHE_HOME), be created with mode 0600, never listen on TCP, authenticate clients by uid (SO_PEERCRED / getpeereid), validate that requested paths are inside the served repository, and refuse to serve when the repository root changes. Acceptance adds: ::test_daemon_socket_permissions, ::test_daemon_rejects_outside_paths.

## Hook integration (added in refinement round 3)
The Claude Code on-file-write hook (F3), the git pre-commit hook and the Cursor/Codex guardrail commands call `ubs --client <files>` when a daemon socket exists and fall back to one-shot `ubs <files>` otherwise, so users get the sub-100 ms path without changing their configuration. Acceptance adds ::test_hook_uses_daemon_when_present.
## Testing and logging requirements (apply to every bead)
- Unit tests live under test-suite/quality/ (Python, unittest, run by test-suite/run_all.sh) or test-suite/shareable/ for meta-runner behaviour; installer tests under test-suite/install/run_tests.sh. Every test prints a `[case-id] RUN/PASS/FAIL (elapsed)` line and, on failure, the full stdout/stderr it captured, so a swarm agent can diagnose from the log alone.
- E2E scripts must run the real `./ubs` (or the real module) against real fixture files with `--ci --format=json`, assert on exact rule ids / counts, and write artifacts under test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/ (stdout.log, stderr.log, result.json).
- Any change to modules/ubs-*.sh or modules/helpers/* must be followed by `./scripts/update_checksums.sh` and `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`; the CI drift check will flag modules against the last tag until the next release is cut (see the cut-release bead).
- Run `shellcheck -S warning` on touched shell files and `./ubs <touched files> --ci` before closing.
acceptance_criteria: - test_daemon.py: start daemon, warm, modify one file, client returns in < 100 ms with identical findings to a one-shot scan; daemon exits after idle timeout.

title: K5: --format=sarif parity — every finding the text/json report carries appears in SARIF for every module (heuristic findings included); contract check compares counts per module
description:
## What
Observed 2026-09-03: `ubs test-suite/python/security/parser_token_compare_buggy.py --format=sarif` returns a SARIF run with 0 results while the same file yields 5 criticals in text/json; a file with ast-grep-backed findings (buggy_async_security.py) yields 10 SARIF results. The Python module's SARIF only carries ast-grep rule hits; heuristic (ripgrep-based) findings are missing. Audit all ten modules: for each fixture pair, count findings in `--format=json` (per-finding records from --report-json where available, otherwise the `findings[].count` sum) against `--format=sarif` results; make SARIF complete (heuristic findings get stable rule ids `<lang>.heuristic.<slug>` with the text's message and the sample line as the region) and add a contract check `sarif_parity_per_module` that scans every language's buggy fixture directory in both formats and asserts sarif results ≥ json finding count − documented exclusions (none expected).

## Why
SARIF is the format GitHub code scanning, IDEs and the shareable reports consume (bead B5 added permalinks to SARIF locations); an agent or reviewer looking at SARIF today silently sees a fraction of what text mode shows. K2 (7qy7.2, per-finding records in json) is the sibling: both need each module to keep one in-memory finding list and render all formats from it (which the A4 ports do by construction — coordinate: for modules ported first, this is free; for the rest it is a module-side change).

## How
1. Script the audit (test-suite/shareable/test_sarif_parity.py, also usable ad hoc): per language, run buggy fixtures in json and sarif; print a table lang | json findings | sarif results | missing rule ids; the contract check is the same script in assert mode.
2. Fix modules where SARIF misses findings (python first — the observed case; then the rest per the table); minimal_sarif_from_text in the meta-runner is the fallback for modules with no native SARIF and must not be the reason for parity (B10 deletes it later).
3. Manifest `sarif` expectations (min_runs/min_results already supported by run_manifest.py) for every language's buggy case.

## Acceptance Criteria
- test_sarif_parity green for all 10 languages; the shareable SARIF permalink check still 100%; CHANGELOG.

## Testing and logging requirements (apply to every bead)
- Unit tests live under test-suite/quality/ (Python, unittest, run by test-suite/run_all.sh) or test-suite/shareable/ for meta-runner behaviour; installer tests under test-suite/install/run_tests.sh. Every test prints a `[case-id] RUN/PASS/FAIL (elapsed)` line and, on failure, the full stdout/stderr it captured, so a swarm agent can diagnose from the log alone.
- E2E checks run the real `./ubs` (or the real module) against real fixture files with `--ci --format=json`, assert on exact rule ids / counts, and write artifacts under test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/.
- Any change to modules/ubs-*.sh, modules/helpers/* or modules/lib/* must be followed by `./scripts/update_checksums.sh` and `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`; any change to `ubs` or `install.sh` by `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`.
- Run `shellcheck -S warning` on touched shell files, `python3 scripts/check_docs_claims.py`, and `./ubs <touched files> --ci` before closing. Gates must run on a frozen tree with no other scans in flight (cargo's global lock and the module timeout checks are load-sensitive).
- Never close on a self-report: cite the gate output (run_all.sh, cli-contract, manifest case ids) in the closing comment, and name anything that could not be verified here (e.g. a CI job on a platform this box does not have).

title: Epic E: Supply chain fail-closed end to end
description:
## Background (reality check 2026-09-02, UBS v5.3.13)
The reality check compared README/AGENTS claims with the code and measured behaviour: 440/440 manifest cases pass, but single-file scans take 4.6–5.8 s (README says < 1 s), a 29K-line fixture tree takes 40 s (README: 3.2 s for 50K lines), a 124K-line Python project takes 143 s, and a 407K-line TypeScript tree hits the 300 s module timeout with 840 MB RSS. The project fails its own gate (`./ubs . --ci` → 9 critical findings, all false positives of the Python constant-time-compare detector). Ten modules are copy-pasted siblings with drifted primitives, five documented meta-runner flags do not exist, inline suppression and severity normalisation are implemented in one module each, helper checksum mismatches fail open during scans, the installer aborts on a clean first install, the Claude Code save hook is never registered, and the docs (AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, modules/README.md, README) drift from the code.

## Goal
docs/security.md promises "invalid checksums fail closed". Make it true for every executable byte UBS runs: modules, helpers, the shared library and core package, dependency binaries fetched by the installer, and the installer's own inputs — and prove it with tamper tests. Make releases impossible to cut with drifted checksums by giving the project one release script.

## Evidence
During a scan a helper checksum mismatch warns, re-downloads and continues with "reduced accuracy" (ubs:2352-2371) — fail-open. Modules never verify helpers themselves (9 call sites do `[[ -f "$helper" ]] && python3 "$helper"`), so `bash modules/ubs-python.sh .` executes helpers with no integrity check. SHA256SUMS covers only ubs and install.sh. install.sh prefers an unverified ./ubs in the current directory over the release-pinned verified artifact (install.sh:2584). ast-grep/ripgrep/jq/typos binaries are downloaded by the installer without checksum verification. Version-tag checksum drift auto-issues fired three times in three weeks (#83, #86, #97) because module changes on main outrun tags.


## Acceptance Criteria
All child beads closed with their acceptance tests green in CI; the epic's 'Done when' statement verified by a fresh scan and documented in CHANGELOG.

## Testing and logging requirements (apply to every bead)
- Unit tests live under test-suite/quality/ (Python, unittest, run by test-suite/run_all.sh) or test-suite/shareable/ for meta-runner behaviour; installer tests under test-suite/install/run_tests.sh. Every test prints a `[case-id] RUN/PASS/FAIL (elapsed)` line and, on failure, the full stdout/stderr it captured, so a swarm agent can diagnose from the log alone.
- E2E scripts must run the real `./ubs` (or the real module) against real fixture files with `--ci --format=json`, assert on exact rule ids / counts, and write artifacts under test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/ (stdout.log, stderr.log, result.json).
- Any change to modules/ubs-*.sh or modules/helpers/* must be followed by `./scripts/update_checksums.sh` and `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`; the CI drift check will flag modules against the last tag until the next release is cut (see the cut-release bead).
- Run `shellcheck -S warning` on touched shell files and `./ubs <touched files> --ci` before closing.

## Success Criteria
Tamper tests refuse modified modules/helpers/lib/binaries; scan-mode mismatch exits 2; cut-release.sh is the only release path and the drift check never fires after a release.

title: Sort the merged top-level findings so report order is stable
description:
The order of the top-level `findings` array in `--format=json` changes from run to run on the same input. With three Python files (`a_first.py` and `z_last.py` each holding one `eval(input())`, and a `m_callbacks.py` that exhausts the taint work limit), ten runs of `ubs <dir> --only=python --ci --format=json` put `z_last.py`'s taint row first in 8 to 9 of them and `a_first.py`'s first in the rest. This held on 14343158, 607712f9 and 7869d7dd. The runner sorts `files` and `counts` (`ubs`, the merge step) but not `findings`, and no doc promises an order.

`test_cli_bounds_natural_callback_context_explosion_without_losing_other_files` asserted the order and so failed most runs; v5.5.26 compares those rows as a sorted list instead.

Follow-up: sort the merged top-level findings by file, line, then rule id next to the existing `files`/`counts` sort, so JSON, SARIF and text output are stable for diffing and caching. Done when ten runs of the scenario above give one order, the test can go back to an ordered comparison, and the golden/report tests pass.

The follow-up is the refactor d02f8607 made for the C# flow policy hooks: pass one record per call shape instead of 7 to 11 parameters, then remove the marker at that site.

- `analyzers/taint_java_traversal.py`: `adapter_graph`
- `java_detectors/archive_extraction.py`: `adapter_graph`, with the same signature as the one above, so one record can serve both

- `analyzers/taint_py.py`: `substitute_binding`

title: Epic H: Test infrastructure and CI — one workflow, sharding, matrix, goldens bot, stronger assertions
description:
## Background (reality check 2026-09-02, UBS v5.3.13)
The reality check compared README/AGENTS claims with the code and measured behaviour: 440/440 manifest cases pass, but single-file scans take 4.6–5.8 s (README says < 1 s), a 29K-line fixture tree takes 40 s (README: 3.2 s for 50K lines), a 124K-line Python project takes 143 s, and a 407K-line TypeScript tree hits the 300 s module timeout with 840 MB RSS. The project fails its own gate (`./ubs . --ci` → 9 critical findings, all false positives of the Python constant-time-compare detector). Ten modules are copy-pasted siblings with drifted primitives, five documented meta-runner flags do not exist, inline suppression and severity normalisation are implemented in one module each, helper checksum mismatches fail open during scans, the installer aborts on a clean first install, the Claude Code save hook is never registered, and the docs (AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, modules/README.md, README) drift from the code.

## Goal
Turn the (excellent) fixture suite into a suite that also proves the meta-runner, installer and supply-chain behaviours, runs fast (sharded), runs on three OSes, and cannot go quietly red: the "UBS Test Suite" workflow was red from 2026-08-17 to 2026-09-02 because of a stale golden, and during that window a regression (JS --format=sarif failing with a duplicate rule id) shipped unnoticed in v5.3.12/13.

## Evidence
ci.yml/manifest.yml/test-suite.yml overlap heavily and run serially (manifest: 440 cases, 32 min); 213/440 cases assert totals only; exactly one case pins a rule id; zero tests for --diff, --beads-jsonl, --format=jsonl, --rules, doctor --fix, tampered-module refusal, ast-grep provisioning; installer tests never run; shellcheck gate is -S error only; all jobs are ubuntu-latest.


## Acceptance Criteria
All child beads closed with their acceptance tests green in CI; the epic's 'Done when' statement verified by a fresh scan and documented in CHANGELOG.

## Testing and logging requirements (apply to every bead)
- Unit tests live under test-suite/quality/ (Python, unittest, run by test-suite/run_all.sh) or test-suite/shareable/ for meta-runner behaviour; installer tests under test-suite/install/run_tests.sh. Every test prints a `[case-id] RUN/PASS/FAIL (elapsed)` line and, on failure, the full stdout/stderr it captured, so a swarm agent can diagnose from the log alone.
- E2E scripts must run the real `./ubs` (or the real module) against real fixture files with `--ci --format=json`, assert on exact rule ids / counts, and write artifacts under test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/ (stdout.log, stderr.log, result.json).
- Any change to modules/ubs-*.sh or modules/helpers/* must be followed by `./scripts/update_checksums.sh` and `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`; the CI drift check will flag modules against the last tag until the next release is cut (see the cut-release bead).

One workflow with sharded manifest and OS matrix under 12 min for PRs; goldens bot in place; no totals-only security cases; nightly full-scope job green.

title: H9: run_all.sh fails when a test leaves new untracked files in the repository (repo-root hygiene guard)
description:
## What
Add a hygiene guard to test-suite/run_all.sh: snapshot `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` (paths only) before the gates, compare after every `run_step`, and fail the run — naming the step and the paths — when a step created untracked files outside test-suite/artifacts/ and the scratch locations tests are allowed to use. Do NOT delete anything (RULE 1); the guard only reports.

## Why (observed defect)
On 2026-09-02 the robot-docs flags-parse contract check ran `ubs --report-json`/`--html-report` with the repository as cwd and left findings.jsonl, report.html, report.json and summary.json at the repo root; nobody noticed until `git status` was read hours later. Tests that write into the checkout can also be picked up by the self-scan and by other agents' auto-commits. A guard that names the offending step turns this into a red gate instead of an archaeology exercise.

## How
1. run_all.sh: `snapshot_untracked()` → sorted list to a temp file; after each step diff against the previous snapshot; allowed prefixes: `test-suite/artifacts/`, `test-suite/goldens/` (when regenerating), `.beads/`; anything else → `❌ [<step>] left untracked files: <list>` and mark the run failed (the step itself keeps its own result).
2. Also compare `git diff --name-only` for tracked files modified by a step that is not expected to modify them (goldens regeneration is the only legitimate case; gate it behind the existing UPDATE_GOLDENS-style env if present) — report only, same shape.
3. Quality unit test: a fake step that touches `stray.txt` in a temporary git repo is reported and the run exits 1; a step that writes only under test-suite/artifacts/ passes.
4. CHANGELOG entry; AGENTS.md testing section: "tests must not write into the checkout except test-suite/artifacts/".

## Acceptance Criteria
- `run_all.sh` green on the current tree; the unit test proves detection; the planted stray file is reported with its step name.

## Testing and logging requirements (apply to every bead)
- Unit tests live under test-suite/quality/ (Python, unittest, run by test-suite/run_all.sh) or test-suite/shareable/ for meta-runner behaviour; installer tests under test-suite/install/run_tests.sh. Every test prints a `[case-id] RUN/PASS/FAIL (elapsed)` line and, on failure, the full stdout/stderr it captured, so a swarm agent can diagnose from the log alone.
- E2E checks run the real `./ubs` (or the real module) against real fixture files with `--ci --format=json`, assert on exact rule ids / counts, and write artifacts under test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/.
- Any change to modules/ubs-*.sh, modules/helpers/* or modules/lib/* must be followed by `./scripts/update_checksums.sh` and `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`; any change to `ubs` or `install.sh` by `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`.
- Run `shellcheck -S warning` on touched shell files, `python3 scripts/check_docs_claims.py`, and `./ubs <touched files> --ci` before closing. Gates must run on a frozen tree with no other scans in flight (cargo's global lock and the module timeout checks are load-sensitive).
- Never close on a self-report: cite the gate output (run_all.sh, cli-contract, manifest case ids) in the closing comment, and name anything that could not be verified here (e.g. a CI job on a platform this box does not have).
close_reason: done

Mode: UBS_TEST_HYGIENE=strict|warn; default strict when CI is set (a step that wrote into the checkout fails the run via FAILED_STEPS), warn otherwise — deliberate deviation from the bead's 'fail the run': on this box other agents create files in the checkout while the suite runs and a red gate would blame the wrong step. title: Epic B: Meta-runner truthfulness — documented CLI surface, file-list pipeline, error envelope
description:
## Background (reality check 2026-09-02, UBS v5.3.13)
The reality check compared README/AGENTS claims with the code and measured behaviour: 440/440 manifest cases pass, but single-file scans take 4.6–5.8 s (README says < 1 s), a 29K-line fixture tree takes 40 s (README: 3.2 s for 50K lines), a 124K-line Python project takes 143 s, and a 407K-line TypeScript tree hits the 300 s module timeout with 840 MB RSS. The project fails its own gate (`./ubs . --ci` → 9 critical findings, all false positives of the Python constant-time-compare detector). Ten modules are copy-pasted siblings with drifted primitives, five documented meta-runner flags do not exist, inline suppression and severity normalisation are implemented in one module each, helper checksum mismatches fail open during scans, the installer aborts on a clean first install, the Claude Code save hook is never registered, and the docs (AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, modules/README.md, README) drift from the code.

## Goal
Make `ubs` do exactly what README documents and nothing surprising: implement the five documented-but-missing flags (OUTPUT_FILE, --include-ext, --rules, --no-color, --list-categories), give --exclude its documented path-glob meaning (languages move to --exclude-langs), reject unknown flags and formats with exit 2, honour the CI env var for auto-update, make FORCE_SELF_UPDATE and UBS_SKIP_TYPE_NARROWING real, replace the whole-tree shadow copy with one NUL file list per language (which also fixes the size guard refusing `--only=js` on a monorepo because of unrelated data), add the machine-readable error envelope for timeouts/env errors, and add fingerprint-based `--new-only` baselines.

## Evidence
`ubs --include-ext=js .` → "scan target not found: --include-ext=js" (exit 2); `ubs . report.txt` scans report.txt instead of writing it; `--exclude=legacy` excludes nothing (ubs:552 treats it as languages); `CI=true` does not disable auto-update (ubs:2441 only tests CI_MODE); FORCE_SELF_UPDATE is hard-coded 0 (ubs:313); UBS_SKIP_TYPE_NARROWING from the environment is overwritten (ubs:3176); a timed-out JS module was reported as `critical: 1, files: 0` with exit 0; `--only=js` on a 1.1 GB tree was refused by the size guard although the JS files were a fraction of it.

title: B11: Explicit-target and git workspaces fall back to tar/python when rsync is missing (Git Bash has none)
description:
## What
`prepare_files_workspace` (explicit file/directory targets: `ubs a.py b.py`, `--files`) and `prepare_git_workspace` (`--staged`, `--diff`) hard-require rsync: without it they print "rsync not found; required for explicit target scans" and exit 1. The whole-project path already falls back rsync → tar → python (apply_ignore_filters), and the list-driven copy landed on 2026-09-03 has the same three tiers. Give the two targeted-workspace builders the same fallbacks, driven by their NUL/newline file lists.

## Why
Git for Windows (the README's advertised Windows path) ships bash 5 and coreutils but NO rsync, so every multi-file, directory-target, `--staged` or `--diff` scan fails there today. The windows-smoke CI job (bead G4) only survives because the single-file fast path (bead C3, `prepare_single_file_target`) needs no copy. macOS has rsync 2.6.9 (old but fine). The fallbacks are cheap: `tar -cf - --null -T list | tar -xf -` and a 15-line python copy loop, both already written for apply_ignore_filters — factor them into one helper `copy_file_list SRC_ROOT LIST DEST` and call it from all three builders.

## How
1. In `ubs`, extract the list-driven copy (rsync `--from0 --files-from`, tar `--null -T`, python shutil loop) from `apply_ignore_filters` into `copy_file_list src list dest` returning 0 on success and printing which tier was used at `say` level; keep `report_rsync_failure` for rsync's stderr.
2. `prepare_files_workspace`: write the resolved file list NUL-separated (today it is newline-separated for `--files-from`; NUL is needed for names with newlines and matches the whole-project list) and call `copy_file_list`; directory targets keep their per-directory copy but through the same helper (list them with rg or find `-print0`).
3. `prepare_git_workspace`: same (it already reads NUL-separated names from git).
4. Remove the two "rsync not found" exits; if all three tiers fail, exit 1 with the existing diagnostics.
5. Contract checks (test_cli_contract.py): `explicit_targets_without_rsync` and `staged_without_rsync` — run with a PATH that has no rsync (a shim dir with bash, coreutils, python3, jq, rg symlinked; PATH=shim only) and assert the scan completes with the same totals as with rsync, and stderr names the tier ("tar fallback"/"python fallback").
6. README "Working files" section: state that rsync is optional everywhere.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The two new contract checks pass on Linux; manifest totals unchanged (run_all green except environment-caused rust-clean).
- `ubs a.py b.py`, `ubs dir/`, `ubs --staged`, `ubs --diff` succeed with rsync absent from PATH.

title: B4b: Language-scoped default ignores (bin/obj/env) and vendor-layout exclusion (node_modules/.bun, .pnpm, symlinked packages) at both levels
description:
## What
DEFAULT_IGNORES in `ubs` is one flat list applied to every language: `bin`, `obj`, `env` are excluded everywhere, so a Go project with cmd/bin sources, a Python package named env, or a C# repo's `obj` are silently skipped (or in C#'s case correctly skipped, but only by accident). Make those three language-scoped: `obj` only when scanning csharp, `env` only when it is a Python virtualenv (contains pyvenv.cfg or bin/activate), `bin` only when it contains no source files of a selected language. Also exclude vendor layouts that the flat list misses: `node_modules/.bun`, `.pnpm`, `node_modules/.pnpm`, and packages reached through symlinks (rsync -a copies symlinks as links; rg does not follow them; but modules using `find` do) — exclude at the meta-runner list stage (build_scan_file_list) AND pass the same globs to modules via `--exclude` so a module run directly behaves the same. Observed: the JS module scanned node_modules/.bun/… bundles when run on lumera_ai/web/apps (bead B4's original report).

## Why
Bead B4's remaining default-ignore work; B8 (ignore-precedence tests) is blocked on this because the precedence rules must be final before they are pinned by tests.

## How
1. `ubs`: DEFAULT_IGNORES keeps the always-ignored names; new `language_scoped_ignores(lang_list)` adds `obj` for csharp, `env` when the directory looks like a venv (check once per candidate directory: pyvenv.cfg / bin/activate / Scripts/activate.bat), `bin` when it holds no files of the selected languages (rg --files -g '*.{ext...}' bin → empty). Apply in build_scan_file_list (globs) and in the `--exclude` string handed to modules (GLOBAL_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS becomes per-run computed after language selection — move the composition to right after select_langs; the size guard runs earlier, so compute the language-independent part first and re-list only when the scoped part changes the set, or run select_langs before the guard using extension probes on the listed files instead of the workspace).
