Vendor layouts: add `node_modules/.bun`, `.pnpm`, `**/node_modules/.pnpm` to the always list; in build_scan_file_list drop entries that resolve through a symlinked directory (`os.lstat` on each path component is too slow for 100k files — instead collect symlinked directories once via `find -type l` at depth ≤ 4 and prefix-match).
3. Tests: `test_cli_contract.py::check_language_scoped_ignores` (temp tree: go project with bin/main.go → scanned; csharp obj/ → skipped; python env/ with pyvenv.cfg → skipped; a plain `env/config.py` in a Go project → scanned) and `::check_vendor_layouts` (node_modules/.bun/bundle.js and .pnpm/x/y.js never appear in js results; a symlinked package dir is skipped).
4. README "Ignoring paths" section: document the scoping rules and the vendor list; `--suggest-ignore` unchanged.

title: B4c: Per-language --files-from hand-off — the meta-runner's file list feeds contract-v2 modules; the workspace copy is kept only for unported modules
description:
## What
Since 2026-09-03 whole-project scans build one NUL-separated file list (build_scan_file_list: rg --files + ignore globs + binary/data/size filter) and copy exactly those files into the shadow workspace. The modules still walk the workspace themselves. Once a module is ported to contract v2 (the A4 beads 0xjg.4–0xjg.13: it sources modules/lib/ubs-common.sh and lists files through `ubs_list_files --files-from FILE`), the meta-runner should split its list per language (by the extension sets each module declares in modules/contract.json, bead A3b) and pass `--files-from=$TMPDIR_RUN/<lang>.files` with the SOURCE tree as the project dir — no copy at all for that module. Modules that do not advertise v2 keep getting the workspace, built once for all of them.

## Why
This is the rest of bead B4: the copy is the last whole-tree pass per scan (0.5 s on this repo after the list-driven copy, seconds on large monorepos, plus /tmp space), and per-language lists let the size guard and `--only` become language-aware for free (a `--only=js` scan of a 1.1 GB data monorepo counts only JS files).

## How
1. contract.json (A3b) declares per module: `extensions`, `manifest_files` (Cargo.toml, package.json, …) and `contract: 2` once ported; `ubs --help` of a v2 module prints `contract: v2` (A4 acceptance) — detect v2 by `modules/ubs-<lang>.sh --help | grep -q 'contract: v2'` cached per run in $TMPDIR_RUN.

title: B4: File-list pipeline replaces the whole-tree shadow copy; language-aware size guard; vendor-layout detection; new default ignores
description:
## What

title: Runner/Installer: ast-grep version compatibility + PATH validation
description:
Problem:
- ubs pins ast-grep 0.40.1 for JS/TS accuracy (tool-cache auto-provision).
- install.sh binary fallback currently downloads ast-grep 0.18.0 and adds it to PATH.
- ubs preflight currently accepts any PATH ast-grep/sg if '--version' contains 'ast-grep' (no capability check).

Impact:
- On systems where installer uses binary fallback (no brew/cargo), users can end up with an old ast-grep in PATH. ubs will then prefer PATH and may break or misbehave if that version lacks required flags/output contracts (e.g. --json=stream/metaVariables) even though tool-cache would have provided the correct pinned build.

Goal:
- Make JS/TS scanning deterministic and reliable: if PATH ast-grep is unusable/outdated, ubs should ignore it and fall back to the verified tool-cache build.
- Align install.sh fallback download to the same pinned version (or at least a compatible minimum) so offline/locked-down users still get a working ast-grep at install time.

Acceptance criteria:
- ubs only uses PATH ast-grep/sg when it passes the same capability checks as doctor (e.g. 'scan -h' and '--json=stream' support as exercised by modules). Otherwise it auto-provisions (or uses) the tool-cache ast-grep 0.40.1.
- install.sh binary fallback for ast-grep downloads a compatible version and (ideally) warns if it can’t verify compatibility.
- Add/adjust a regression test that simulates a bogus/old 'ast-grep' on PATH and ensures ubs selects tool-cache instead.

title: Add --stats flag for token comparison display
description: When --stats is passed alongside --format=toon, append token savings statistics to the output. This leverages tru --stats which outputs 'Token estimates: ~N (JSON) -> ~M (TOON), Saved ~K tokens (-X.Y%)'. Implementation: pass --stats to the tru invocation when this flag is set.

title: modules/ubs-js.sh: fail fast (env error) instead of regex fallback on TS/TSX
description: When ast-grep isn't usable, the JS module prints 'regex fallback mode' and continues, which can explode into dozens of false positives on TSX/TypeScript syntax. Change default behavior: if TS/TSX/JSX is present and no AST engine is available, stop and return an explicit environment error.

title: JS/TS: fix global-pollution heuristic false positives (JSX props, default params, TS syntax)
description: The 'Global variable assignments' detector in modules/ubs-js.sh uses a regex-based Python heuristic that can misinterpret valid TS/TSX syntax (multiline JSX props and default parameters) as top-level assignments, producing bogus criticals/warnings.

title: JS/TS: AST-confirm high-severity regex findings before reporting
description: Even with ast-grep installed, some UBS JS checks are regex/heuristic-based and can produce false positives on TS/TSX syntax. For the highest-severity findings (CRITICAL/WARNING), add a lightweight AST confirmation step so we only report matches that correspond to real syntax nodes.
notes:
Initial audit:
- Some CRITICAL/WARNING checks in `modules/ubs-js.sh` still use ripgrep regex counts even when ast-grep is available.
- This causes:
  - False positives / miscounts from matches in comments/strings (e.g., `debugger` mentioned in comments).
  - A real coverage gap: the current typeof check only matches `typeof(<expr>)` (paren form) and misses the common `typeof x === 'array'` form used in fixtures.

Implementation plan:
1) Add ast-grep-backed counting + sample output helpers (so high-sev findings show real syntax nodes).
2) Convert at least these high-sev rules to AST when available:
   - Direct NaN comparisons (==/===/!=/!== with NaN on either side)
   - Loose equality (== / != binary expressions)
   - Invalid typeof comparisons (typeof comparisons to invalid string literals; include both paren + non-paren, and handle yoda form)
   - debugger statements (debugger statement node)
3) Add a manifest regression case that ensures invalid typeof comparisons are detected (and not dependent on parenthesized typeof).

title: modules/ubs-js.sh: honor UBS_AST_GREP_BIN for AST engine
description: To enable ubs-level tool caching (and avoid PATH issues), the JS module should accept an explicit ast-grep binary path via env var and use it preferentially when valid.

title: JS/TS: guarantee AST scanning + eliminate TSX regex-fallback false positives
description: When UBS runs on TS/TSX projects it can fall back to regex/heuristic scanning and produce large numbers of false positives (e.g., multiline JSX attributes and default parameters misread as assignments/comparisons). This epic makes JS/TS scanning syntax-aware by default (ast-grep always available/used) and defines a strict degraded-mode policy so we never spam users with bogus CRITICAL/WARNING counts.

title: Spec: JS/TS degraded-mode policy when AST engine is unavailable
description: Define the contract for how UBS behaves when JS/TS scanning cannot use a syntax-aware engine (ast-grep or equivalent). The goal is: never emit large bogus CRITICAL/WARNING counts from regex fallback; treat missing AST as an environment error with clear remediation.

title: JS/TS: inventory TS/TSX false positives + map to scanners
description: Before changing behavior, build a precise map from reported false positives to the exact UBS JS module checks that emitted them (regex/heuristic vs ast-grep). This prevents us from fixing the wrong layer and accidentally reducing real bug coverage.

title: Epic J: Documentation truth and process — generated docs, claim checker, release script, beads hygiene
description:
## Background (reality check 2026-09-02, UBS v5.3.13)
The reality check compared README/AGENTS claims with the code and measured behaviour: 440/440 manifest cases pass, but single-file scans take 4.6–5.8 s (README says < 1 s), a 29K-line fixture tree takes 40 s (README: 3.2 s for 50K lines), a 124K-line Python project takes 143 s, and a 407K-line TypeScript tree hits the 300 s module timeout with 840 MB RSS. The project fails its own gate (`./ubs . --ci` → 9 critical findings, all false positives of the Python constant-time-compare detector). Ten modules are copy-pasted siblings with drifted primitives, five documented meta-runner flags do not exist, inline suppression and severity normalisation are implemented in one module each, helper checksum mismatches fail open during scans, the installer aborts on a clean first install, the Claude Code save hook is never registered, and the docs (AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, modules/README.md, README) drift from the code.

## Goal
Docs are the measuring stick for agents; today they overstate the code. Correct the drift now, then make the README/AGENTS/SKILL sections that describe flags, languages, helpers, versions, exit codes, performance and coverage *generated* from code and benchmarks, with a CI check that fails on any documented flag the binary does not accept.

## Evidence
AGENTS.md: "currently 5.0.7" (actual 5.3.13), "9 languages" (10), lists 10 helpers (14 exist), omits scripts/check-version-tag-drift.sh, exit-code table lacks 2 and 3, instructs pushing to `master` while also forbidding references to master. SKILL.md: "8 languages", "18 detection categories", documents `ubs:ignore-next-line` (unsupported). modules/README.md: no elixir, no jsonl/toon, no --list-rules/--dump-rules. README: title "v5.0", banner "v4.4", "No temp files created" (every scan copies the tree to a shadow workspace), "Memory usage: <100MB" (840 MB measured), performance table 3–14× optimistic, uninstall one-liner cannot work, --exclude semantics wrong, agent blurb exit codes omit 2/3, "normalize_severity() in each module" (1/10), "works across all 10 languages" for suppression placements (JS only), Docker image limitations undocumented.


## Acceptance Criteria
All child beads closed with their acceptance tests green in CI; the epic's 'Done when' statement verified by a fresh scan and documented in CHANGELOG.

## Testing and logging requirements (apply to every bead)
- Unit tests live under test-suite/quality/ (Python, unittest, run by test-suite/run_all.sh) or test-suite/shareable/ for meta-runner behaviour; installer tests under test-suite/install/run_tests.sh. Every test prints a `[case-id] RUN/PASS/FAIL (elapsed)` line and, on failure, the full stdout/stderr it captured, so a swarm agent can diagnose from the log alone.
- E2E scripts must run the real `./ubs` (or the real module) against real fixture files with `--ci --format=json`, assert on exact rule ids / counts, and write artifacts under test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/ (stdout.log, stderr.log, result.json).
- Any change to modules/ubs-*.sh or modules/helpers/* must be followed by `./scripts/update_checksums.sh` and `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`; the CI drift check will flag modules against the last tag until the next release is cut (see the cut-release bead).
- Run `shellcheck -S warning` on touched shell files and `./ubs <touched files> --ci` before closing.

## Success Criteria
check-docs-claims.sh green in CI; every generated doc section current; beads tracker healthy with no stale or duplicate open beads.

title: Infra: Set up toon_rust GitHub releases with platform binaries
description:
## Task

Configure toon_rust repository to publish pre-built `tru` binaries for all supported platforms via GitHub releases.

## Required Release Assets

For each release (e.g., v0.1.1), publish:
- `tru-linux-amd64.tar.xz` - Linux AMD64
- `tru-linux-arm64.tar.xz` - Linux ARM64
- `tru-darwin-amd64.tar.xz` - macOS Intel
- `tru-darwin-arm64.tar.xz` - macOS Apple Silicon
- `tru-windows-amd64.zip` - Windows AMD64
- `*.sha256` files for each asset

## Implementation Options

1. **GitHub Actions workflow** (recommended)
   - Cross-compile on release tag push
   - Use `cross` for Linux targets
   - Native build for macOS via matrix

2. **Manual release process**
   - Document build commands for each platform
   - Less ideal but works

## Binary Naming

The binary inside the archive should be named `tru` (not `tr`) to:
- Avoid conflict with Unix `tr` command
- Make purpose clear
- Allow safe PATH inclusion

## Archive Structure

```
tru-linux-amd64.tar.xz
└── tru  (the binary)
```

## Reference

See how ast-grep does releases:
https://github.com/ast-grep/ast-grep/releases

## Dependencies

None - can be done in parallel with other work.

## Notes

This work happens in the toon_rust repository, not ultimate_bug_scanner.
The UBS installer will consume these release assets.

title: Core: Auto-configure TOON_BIN in ubs script
description:
## Task

Modify the ubs script to automatically detect and use the installed `tru` binary without requiring user configuration.

## Current State

```bash
# In ubs script (line ~147)
# TOON_BIN should default to tru (toon_rust); Node `toon` is forbidden
```

## Proposed Change

```bash
# Auto-detect toon_rust binary location (no Node.js fallback)
detect_toon_bin() {
  local candidates=(
    "$HOME/.local/bin/tru"     # Standard install location
    "$HOME/.cargo/bin/tru"     # Cargo install location
    "/usr/local/bin/tru"       # System-wide install
  )
  for bin in "${candidates[@]}"; do
    if [[ -x "$bin" ]]; then
      echo "$bin"
      return 0
    fi
  done
  # Fall back to PATH lookup
  if command -v tru >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v tru
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

# Resolution order: TOON_TRU_BIN > TOON_BIN > tru (PATH)
TOON_BIN="${TOON_TRU_BIN:-${TOON_BIN:-tru}}"
```

## Why This Approach

1. **Zero user configuration** - Works out of box after installation
2. **Respects user override** - TOON_TRU_BIN/TOON_BIN env var still works
3. **No Node.js fallback** - Only toon_rust encoder is accepted
4. **Multiple install locations** - Supports different installation methods

## Location

Modify ubs script near line 147 where TOON_BIN is defined.

## Dependencies

- bd-3a6.4 (Core: integration - binary must be installed first)

## Testing

- Fresh install: should auto-detect ~/.local/bin/tru
- Manual override: TOON_TRU_BIN=/custom/path should work
- Missing tru: should warn and fall back to JSON output (no Node.js)

title: Test: Verify toon_rust installation on Linux and macOS
description:
## Task

Create and execute comprehensive tests for toon_rust binary installation across all supported platforms.

## Test Matrix

| Platform | Architecture | Test Environment |
|----------|--------------|------------------|
| Linux | x86_64 | GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest |
| Linux | aarch64 | GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest (qemu) or self-hosted |
| macOS | x86_64 | GitHub Actions macos-13 |
| macOS | aarch64 | GitHub Actions macos-latest (M1) |

## Test Cases

### 1. Fresh Installation
```bash
# Clean environment (no existing ubs)
./install.sh
# Verify: ~/.local/bin/tru exists and is executable
# Verify: ubs --format=toon produces TOON output
```

### 2. Binary Verification
```bash
tru --version  # Should show toon_rust version
echo "{\"test\":1}" | tru  # Should produce TOON output
```

### 3. Integration Test
```bash
ubs --format=toon test-suite/buggy 2>&1 | grep -q "project:"
# Should use tru (check stderr for "Rust" or timing)
```

### 4. Fallback Test (no tru)
```bash
mv ~/.local/bin/tru ~/.local/bin/tru.bak
ubs --format=toon test-suite/buggy  # Should warn + fall back to JSON output (no Node)
```

### 5. Performance Comparison
```bash
time ubs --format=toon . > /dev/null  # With toon_rust
TOON_DEFAULT_FORMAT=json time ubs . > /dev/null  # Baseline JSON
# TOON should be faster and smaller than JSON output
```

## CI Integration

Add to existing GitHub Actions workflow or create new test-installer.yml:
```yaml
jobs:
  test-install:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, macos-13]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: ./install.sh
      - run: ~/.local/bin/tru --version
      - run: ./ubs --format=toon test-suite/buggy
```

## Dependencies

- bd-3a6.5 (Core: auto-configure - full implementation must be complete)

## Deliverables

- Test script or CI workflow
- Test results for all platforms
- Performance benchmarks

Distinguish file objects from raw POSIX descriptors and recognize real ownership transfer/cleanup. Keep unclosed os.open descriptors reported, including fake/conditional cleanup and fdopen(closefd=False).

Actual prior scanner and candidate run against same real clean/leaking fixtures in one invocation; safe DSR reader becomes warning-free while actual descriptor leaks remain warning findings. Existing Python precision/completion and full scanner gates retain their checks.

## Objective and current reality
User-requested October 6 comprehensive reality-check and idea-wizard bridge. UBS's twelve real CLI modules, shared contract/finding pipeline, integrity checks and tested service/editor paths work, but default semantic depth is uneven. Local evidence at scanner code 40cc563: manifest 490/490; core 427/427; focused semantics 350 pass/four optional skips; all twelve native SARIF envelopes parse; project self-scan zero critical/warning with 6054 info. This does not certify empirical precision, an unmodified full run_all.sh, cleanup/uninstall, all platforms or published current features.

## Concrete defects and highest priority
Advertised Python 3.9 fails eagerly imported JS @dataclass(slots=True), confirmed CI 37518311400/37518311268. Actual native CLI misses unsafe Java/Ruby/Swift/Elixir identity helpers when named safe-looking; ordinary renaming to identity restores one critical target finding each. Java/Ruby fixed-literal overwrites still trigger criticals. Ruby's actual threads.each(&:join) example yields an unjoined-thread warning. Some mature AST/guard/narrowing code is advisory or default-off without ordinary CLI exposure. Exact prescribed ShellCheck exits 1 on info/style diagnostics. These need independently authored probes and fixes, not new headings, a weakened gate, changed expectations or closed-count progress.

## Delivery and proof gaps
Published v5.4.17 lacks daemon/Sigstore assets; checkout is 5.4.23. Main CI/Test Suite/Release are disabled_manually. Existing G6/H8/E5/F7 own release/platform/user journeys. D7 owns honest held-out accuracy/confidence and statistical gates; J1 owns real active/advisory/gated/unavailable capability provenance and docs, not a second metrics program. C6/C7/K4 own bounded streaming, current benchmark tables and changed-source <100ms, not another daemon. The old plan's repository scan configuration is not implemented by installer defaults or session --config-dir.

## Selected feature plan
Reuse shared taint_flow and existing Python AST, JS selected modules/heap facts, Go package/decoder facts, Rust scoped summaries and C# helper-body/guard proof in receiver-specific JVM, Ruby, Swift, Elixir and C/C++ slices. Give Kotlin native coroutine/cancellation/null semantics; resource use{} belongs to its distinct handle ownership slice. Qualify dormant checks individually, improve per-binding resource/task obligations, then port SQL binding, framework configuration, deadlines, crypto identity and native outcome semantics. Add bounded PHP first, PostgreSQL SQL and provider-aware HCL next; PowerShell/Dart/Lua remain deferred ecosystem options, not immediate graph proliferation. Optional persistent scan config is lower-priority bridge work.

## Dependency and acceptance discipline
Each new implementation is blocked on its independently authored unit/CLI probe. Probe-authoring closure requires real baseline evidence and an independently sound oracle, not a feature pass; implementation closure requires the same fixed-behavior tests green with cited artifacts. There is no reciprocal implementation/probe dependency and no arbitrary cross-receiver blocking chain. Shared future edit surfaces need reservations. Existing owner/status information is preserved; this planning audit closes no implementation work.
Every task is self-contained: problem, donor/receiver files, scope/limits, API-specific acceptance examples, exact public IDs/locations/exits, comments/strings/shadowing/unrelated scopes, failure/budget states and applicable suppression/profile/selection/cache-context controls. Real JSON/SARIF E2Es log command/source/tool/policy/run identities, timings and full stdout/stderr under test-suite/artifacts/. Future code edits are manual, checksum/version/release policies apply and no files may be deleted without exact written permission.
Closure of this epic requires every selected implementation's named probe, existing reused accuracy/docs/release/performance target evidence, a coherent effective capability record and explicit remaining/deferred scope. Plan/report/graph edits are not implementation progress, self-speedup is maintenance, and a live incumbent in the same invocation is required for competitive performance claims. Keep br dependency cycles empty.

HCL is an unserved infrastructure ecosystem and has a usable ast-grep grammar. Syntax alone does not establish network exposure or deployed provider defaults.

## Donor/receiver surfaces
new modules/ubs-hcl.sh and HCL/Terraform helper, common scaffold/contract, ubs detection, modules/contract.json, test-suite/hcl and manifest.json, modules/helpers/ubs_core/registry.py and analyzers/__init__.py when registering a new analyzer

## Implementation and adaptation
Implement provider/resource-specific first slices for literal insecure network ingress, storage public access, IAM wildcard privilege and explicitly disabled TLS verification. Parse .tf and document .tfvars/context treatment. Resolve selected locals/literal expressions, references and contradictory protective settings when supported. Unresolved variables/modules/provider defaults are unknown, never proof of deployed exposure or clean infrastructure. Reuse common output/errors, selected-file behavior, discovery, docs and integrity/version integration. Extend actual analyzer language registration/imports as needed; the module inventory and analyzer registry are distinct and Bash is already a module without a registry language entry.

## Independent acceptance behavior
Real CLI catches explicit supported provider/resource insecure cases and reports precise block/attribute locations. Restricted ingress, provider-appropriate protective defaults, unrelated user blocks, comments/strings, variable indirection, conflicting protective controls and unknown expressions have independent negative/incomplete controls.

## Scope, limits and existing related work
Source-level provider-specific checks; no promise of Terraform plan/state equivalence, all providers, policy compliance certification or automatic deployment changes.
Existing work to reuse and coordinate: ultimate_bug_scanner-jtst.1. These links are context, not artificial blocking edges.

## Named probe and closure
ultimate_bug_scanner-mj1j.35 must author the independent oracle first. This implementation is blocked on that authoring task. Its own completion requires the same fixed-behavior cases green and cited real module/CLI artifacts; probe-authoring closure on an expected-red baseline is not feature completion.

## Implementation discipline and proof
Read repository and suite AGENTS.md. Reserve the selected edit surface and respect the single-writer graph rule. Make code edits manually, extend existing files where possible, create new files only for genuinely new functionality, and never delete files without the user's exact written authorization. Coordinate overlapping donor files; do not rewrite another receiver's work.
Every detector addition needs independent unit tests plus a real-module/meta-runner E2E companion. Positive and safe outcomes must assert exact public rule IDs, selected sink/obligation locations, totals and exits rather than broad substring/count thresholds. Extend existing quality suites and fixtures; artifact writes belong under test-suite/artifacts/. Unit/E2E logs include case ID, command, source/tool identity, elapsed time, exit and complete captured stdout/stderr on failure. Include lexical decoys, shadowing, unrelated scopes, malformed/unsupported input and budget/tool failure; applicable selection/ignore/suppression/profile/cache-context checks are mandatory. Unsupported/exhausted analysis cannot silently mean clean.
After substantive code work, run the prescribed ShellCheck/checksum/full-suite/SHA256SUMS checks and investigate failures without weakening gates or regenerating expectations to bless defects. Module/helper changes require current embedded checksums, version mirrors and verified release/tag handling through the existing release process. Platform/publication proof is not implied by Linux unit success. No scanner work is implemented or closed by the October audit.
Closure requires the named companion probe's cited passing artifact/run and observed coverage boundaries, not self-report or plan edits.

title: Author independent probe: Resolve the prescribed ShellCheck gate with documented callback proof
description:
## Independent probe objective
Author the behavioral regression oracle for: Resolve the prescribed ShellCheck gate with documented callback proof.

## Observed problem and reason
The prescribed shellcheck ubs modules/ubs-*.sh scripts/*.sh returns exit 1 despite zero warning/error diagnostics: 193 info and four style messages, including 155 SC2317 reports for indirect/trap callbacks. A weaker -S warning run is not evidence that the exact prescribed gate passes.

## Real edit/test surfaces and donor context
ubs, modules/ubs-*.sh, scripts/*.sh and existing ShellCheck validation in .github/workflows/ci.yml

## Required behavior and independent safe/unsafe controls
The exact prescribed command passes on the final frozen tree. All previously valid safety findings remain detectable in independent controls. Every annotation names the concrete registered invocation that ShellCheck cannot infer; real callback behavior and error/trap handling stay equivalent. Full CLI/manifest/checksum gates still pass.

## Scope and boundaries
Maintenance repair of a documented gate, not a performance/accuracy win or license to suppress real errors. No claim that zero warnings/errors makes the original command green.
Related existing work: ultimate_bug_scanner-jtst.1, ultimate_bug_scanner-aom8.8. Tests may reuse its harness, but not assume its claimed feature is correct.

## Test and logging contract
Use real source fixtures and actual module/meta-runner invocations, not a mocked analyzer or a duplicate implementation as oracle. Unit tests should independently specify intended language/API semantics; E2E scripts exercise JSON and SARIF with exact expected and forbidden public IDs, locations, totals and exit statuses. Use semantic alpha-renaming only when bindings are preserved; reorder only provably independent statements; regenerate no goldens to hide a failing oracle.
Write case-command/source/tool/hash/environment identity, elapsed time, status and full stdout/stderr to test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/. Keep tests within allowed artifact/golden write locations and obey no-deletion instructions. Missing optional tools, malformed rules, timeout and analysis-budget exhaustion require explicit evidence, not clean findings. Applicable selected-file/ignore, profile/category, suppression, alias/shadowing, scopes and warm-versus-cold/context invalidation checks must be covered.
Run relevant existing semantic suites, the unmodified manifest and prescribed full checks on a frozen implementation tree. Report remaining platform/dependency/cleanup skips and reasons. Closure only on cited passing evidence; writing this probe specification does not certify the feature.
This bead authors the independent regression oracle before implementation. It may close only after fixtures are semantically reviewed, the real harness runs, and the current known failure/unsupported baseline is captured alongside passing independent harness controls. A documented expected-red feature test is evidence of the starting defect, not a feature pass. Do not commit a weakened/xfail gate or treat this authoring closure as implementation completion. The implementation bead is blocked on this authored probe, and its own closure requires the same exact fixed-behavior cases to pass with cited real CLI artifacts. Attach the final green run here when the implementation is verified.

title: Discharge in-function JVM path-construction effects when target.startsWith(base) guards void-handler sinks
description: In modules/helpers/ubs_core/analyzers/taint_java_traversal.py:646-652 and 856-861, Engine.expression() immediately records a path-construction effect at base.resolve(rel). Engine.summary_effect() discharges that effect when target is returned from a helper method with contained-path in summary.returned, but inside a void handler (where summary.returned is empty), Path target = base.resolve(req.getParameter("file")).normalize(); if (target.startsWith(base)) { Files.readString(target); } falsely fires java.taint.path_traversal on base.resolve(...) (reproduced in test-suite/artifacts/reality-probes-20261013/java_path_clean). Discharge in-function path-construction effects when every downstream use of the constructed Path binding is dominated by a containment guard (or unused outside guarded branches), while keeping unguarded base.resolve/Files.* uses flagged.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Inline Path target = base.resolve(req.getParameter("file")).normalize(); if (target.startsWith(base)) { Files.readString(target); } inside a void servlet/controller method exits 0 with 0 critical findings via modules/ubs-java.sh --format=json. 2. Unguarded Files.readString(target) or sibling-prefix string startsWith remains flagged as java.taint.path_traversal.

title: Author independent probe: Adapt finite flow and validation summaries to Elixir request redirect/path sinks
description:
## Independent probe objective
Author the behavioral regression oracle for: Adapt finite flow and validation summaries to Elixir request redirect/path sinks.

## Observed problem and reason
The actual Elixir CLI returns exit 0 for a request value passed to an identity safe_redirect helper before Phoenix redirect. Current named-safe and nearby-context logic does not establish safe value flow.

## Real edit/test surfaces and donor context
modules/helpers/ubs_core/analyzers/taint_elixir_redirect.py, taint_elixir_traversal.py, elixir_scan.py, elixir_detectors/ and taint_flow.py

## Required behavior and independent safe/unsafe controls
Observed identity bypass is detected; real validated local paths and bounded file paths are clean. Include pipelines, rebinding, multiple clauses, failure branches, unrelated conn variables, keyword arguments, helper shadowing and malformed syntax. No residual file-global taint crosses unrelated functions. The October ordinary-CLI alpha-renaming control changes only the selected helper name from safe-looking to identity and produces one critical target finding; preserve that binding-equivalent metamorphic oracle.

## Scope and boundaries
Selected same-module semantics first. Macros, runtime module dispatch and arbitrary Phoenix/Ecto configuration are explicit boundaries, not clean evidence.
Related existing work: ultimate_bug_scanner-1b9j.6. Tests may reuse its harness, but not assume its claimed feature is correct.

## Test and logging contract
Use real source fixtures and actual module/meta-runner invocations, not a mocked analyzer or a duplicate implementation as oracle. Unit tests should independently specify intended language/API semantics; E2E scripts exercise JSON and SARIF with exact expected and forbidden public IDs, locations, totals and exit statuses. Use semantic alpha-renaming only when bindings are preserved; reorder only provably independent statements; regenerate no goldens to hide a failing oracle.
Write case-command/source/tool/hash/environment identity, elapsed time, status and full stdout/stderr to test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/. Keep tests within allowed artifact/golden write locations and obey no-deletion instructions. Missing optional tools, malformed rules, timeout and analysis-budget exhaustion require explicit evidence, not clean findings. Applicable selected-file/ignore, profile/category, suppression, alias/shadowing, scopes and warm-versus-cold/context invalidation checks must be covered.
Run relevant existing semantic suites, the unmodified manifest and prescribed full checks on a frozen implementation tree. Report remaining platform/dependency/cleanup skips and reasons. Closure only on cited passing evidence; writing this probe specification does not certify the feature.
This bead authors the independent regression oracle before implementation. It may close only after fixtures are semantically reviewed, the real harness runs, and the current known failure/unsupported baseline is captured alongside passing independent harness controls. A documented expected-red feature test is evidence of the starting defect, not a feature pass. Do not commit a weakened/xfail gate or treat this authoring closure as implementation completion. The implementation bead is blocked on this authored probe, and its own closure requires the same exact fixed-behavior cases to pass with cited real CLI artifacts. Attach the final green run here when the implementation is verified.

title: verify.sh: portable SHA256 + version normalization
description: scripts/verify.sh currently hard-depends on GNU sha256sum and its --check mode, which breaks on macOS defaults. It also documents '--version vX.Y.Z' but unconditionally prefixes 'v' in the release URL, causing 'vvX.Y.Z' if users include the leading v. title: Release: restore a dsr repo config for ubs, so the next release goes through dsr instead of being assembled by hand
description:
v5.5.3 was released through dsr: its assets include dsr's `ubs.minisig`, `ubs.sha256` and `ubs-v5.5.3-manifest.json` next to `ubs`, `ubs-daemon`, `install.sh`, `verify.sh`, `git_safety_guard.py`, `ubs.rb`, `minisign.pub`, `sbom.spdx.json`, `SHA256SUMS` and its `.minisig`.

The release machine used for v5.5.26 has no dsr repo config for ubs, so v5.5.26's ten assets were assembled by hand from the tag (`git archive` export, SBOM from syft, `SHA256SUMS` signed with minisign) and uploaded to a draft release. The three dsr-only assets were dropped after a search showed that nothing reads them: not `install.sh`, `ubs`, `verify.sh`, the homebrew formula, or the ACFS installer.

Nothing in ubs compiles, so the config only has to describe script assets, signing and the SBOM, not build targets. Not a blocker for any release.

Done when:
- a dsr repo config for ubs exists that produces the v5.5.26 asset set (the ten files above) from a tag, signs `SHA256SUMS` with the release minisign key, and makes the SBOM;
- a dry run against the v5.5.26 tag reproduces the published assets byte for byte (or each difference is explained);
- it is decided, and written in this bead, whether dsr's `ubs.minisig`, `ubs.sha256` and the manifest come back. If they do, `verify.sh` and the notes say what reads them.

Not in scope: keyless sigstore bundles, SLSA provenance and image signatures, which need a GitHub Actions run.

title: Epic F: Installer correctness — first-run abort, flag order, Claude hooks, uninstall, hygiene
description:
## Background (reality check 2026-09-02, UBS v5.3.13)
The reality check compared README/AGENTS claims with the code and measured behaviour: 440/440 manifest cases pass, but single-file scans take 4.6–5.8 s (README says < 1 s), a 29K-line fixture tree takes 40 s (README: 3.2 s for 50K lines), a 124K-line Python project takes 143 s, and a 407K-line TypeScript tree hits the 300 s module timeout with 840 MB RSS. The project fails its own gate (`./ubs . --ci` → 9 critical findings, all false positives of the Python constant-time-compare detector). Ten modules are copy-pasted siblings with drifted primitives, five documented meta-runner flags do not exist, inline suppression and severity normalisation are implemented in one module each, helper checksum mismatches fail open during scans, the installer aborts on a clean first install, the Claude Code save hook is never registered, and the docs (AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, modules/README.md, README) drift from the code.

## Goal
The installer works on the first run on a clean machine, does what the README says for agent integrations, and uninstalls what it installed.

## Evidence (all verified against install.sh at v5.3.13)
- install.sh:1314 `((errors++))` with errors=0 returns status 1 under `set -Eeuo pipefail`, so verify_installation aborts the whole installer whenever `ubs` is not yet on PATH — the default first install (and any --no-path-modify install). Doctor, session log, PATH-shadow warning, self-test and the success banner never run.
- --uninstall executes at parse position (install.sh:3549) before --non-interactive is seen, so README's documented one-liner `--uninstall --non-interactive` prompts (TTY) or prints "Uninstall cancelled" (no TTY). Same for --setup-git-hook/--setup-claude-hook/--generate-config vs a later --dry-run; --easy-mode does not suppress the update prompt at 3436; --help/--info take the lock and hit the network.
- The Claude Code on-file-write.sh hook is written but never registered in .claude/settings.json and reads $FILE_PATH/$PROJECT_DIR which Claude Code hooks do not set; git_safety_guard.py is never installed (0 references) although README says the installer sets it up.
- TabNine and Replit are detection-only; Copilot writes .github/copilot-instructions.md not "workspace settings".
- --uninstall misses .codex/rules/ubs.md, Continue, Copilot, Aider, the cron job and session.md; the guardrail-removal sed uses markers that the writer never emits (prints success, deletes nothing); the fish alias removal leaves a dangling `end`.
- --dry-run creates the lock dir and ~/.local/bin and appends to session.md; no stale-lock detection; ubs.tmp registered outside WORKDIR leaks on interrupt; dead variables FORCE_UNINSTALL/LOCK_FD/CHECKSUM_SIG_FILE/TYPE_NARROWING_READY; config key skip_bun unknown.
- test-suite/install/run_tests.sh (4 scenarios) is invoked by nothing.


## Acceptance Criteria
All child beads closed with their acceptance tests green in CI; the epic's 'Done when' statement verified by a fresh scan and documented in CHANGELOG.

## Testing and logging requirements (apply to every bead)
- Unit tests live under test-suite/quality/ (Python, unittest, run by test-suite/run_all.sh) or test-suite/shareable/ for meta-runner behaviour; installer tests under test-suite/install/run_tests.sh. Every test prints a `[case-id] RUN/PASS/FAIL (elapsed)` line and, on failure, the full stdout/stderr it captured, so a swarm agent can diagnose from the log alone.
- E2E scripts must run the real `./ubs` (or the real module) against real fixture files with `--ci --format=json`, assert on exact rule ids / counts, and write artifacts under test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/ (stdout.log, stderr.log, result.json).
- Any change to modules/ubs-*.sh or modules/helpers/* must be followed by `./scripts/update_checksums.sh` and `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`; the CI drift check will flag modules against the last tag until the next release is cut (see the cut-release bead).
- Run `shellcheck -S warning` on touched shell files and `./ubs <touched files> --ci` before closing.

## Success Criteria
Installer test suite green on Linux, macOS and Windows from an empty $HOME; Claude hooks registered and firing; uninstall leaves the tree identical.

title: F8: Non-interactive installs provision the toon encoder by default (opt-out --skip-toon); `ubs doctor --fix` installs it from the digest-pinned release
description:
## What
Two gaps left by the toon installer work (epic 3a6, closed children 3a6.3–3a6.5, 3a6.7):
1. `curl … | bash -s -- --non-interactive` (the README's quick install and the Docker/CI paths) does NOT install the encoder: the "Install the toon encoder now?" prompt defaults to no in non-interactive mode, exactly like ripgrep/jq. `--easy-mode` or an interactive yes installs it. Decide and implement: in non-interactive mode install the encoder when the platform has a pinned asset (linux/darwin amd64/arm64, windows amd64), skip with the existing `--skip-toon`; keep the prompt for interactive runs.
2. `ubs doctor --fix` repairs modules, helpers and ast-grep but cannot provision the encoder; it only prints the info line added on 2026-09-03. ## Why
The 3a6 epic's stated goal was "fully automated, zero-config" TOON output; the current behaviour leaves the most common install path (non-interactive) without it, and `doctor --fix` is where users are told to go when something is missing. title: pip-audit dependency audit is hollow: --path <pyproject.toml> audits zero distributions
description:
`modules/ubs-python.sh` runs `pip-audit --path "$PROJECT_DIR/pyproject.toml"` for Python dependency vulnerability coverage (the `pyproject.toml` branch; a `-r requirements.txt` branch is used when a requirements file is present, and `--path "$PROJECT_DIR"` otherwise).

But pip-audit's `--path` selects an *installation path* — a `PipSource` over an installed environment (pip-audit `_cli.py:535-539`, help text "restrict to the specified installation path") — not a project manifest. Pointing `--path` at a `pyproject.toml` *file* yields zero installed distributions, so pip-audit prints "No known vulnerabilities found" while auditing nothing: a hollow pass that provides no dependency coverage, and would miss a real advisory in a declared dependency.

Demonstration (pip-audit 2.10.1, `--dry-run`, which collects dependencies without querying the advisory service):
- `pip-audit --path <repo>/pyproject.toml --dry-run` -> "Dry run: would have audited 0 packages".
- `pip-audit --path <a populated site-packages directory> --dry-run` -> "Dry run: would have audited 28 packages".

This is pre-existing: the `--path "$PROJECT_DIR/pyproject.toml"` invocation is present at tag v5.5.26 (`modules/ubs-python.sh:647`) and on current main. It does not block a release, but the Python dependency audit is silently empty.

Fix: audit the project's resolved dependencies instead of passing a `pyproject.toml` file to `--path` — e.g. prefer the `-r requirements.txt` path when present, or resolve the `pyproject.toml` dependencies into an environment or lockfile and audit that (or audit the installed environment).
close_reason: Resolved project dependencies through requirements.txt or pip-audit's positional project resolver, with explicit skipped/partial coverage and counted native advisories in text/JSON/SARIF. Real pip-audit 2.10.1 dry-run on the same urllib3 fixture: old --path manifest collected 0 packages; project resolver collected 1. PipAuditResults and PythonOptionalIntegration regressions cover input selection, advisory retention, malformed/truncated output, failure/cancellation, package-specific baseline identities and retained scratch. Daemon live audits bypass report reuse in every format. Live advisory-service lookup was time-limited; report contracts use deterministic external fixtures.

title: Epic C: Performance program — measure, prefilter, cache, schedule, stream
description:
## Background (reality check 2026-09-02, UBS v5.3.13)
The reality check compared README/AGENTS claims with the code and measured behaviour: 440/440 manifest cases pass, but single-file scans take 4.6–5.8 s (README says < 1 s), a 29K-line fixture tree takes 40 s (README: 3.2 s for 50K lines), a 124K-line Python project takes 143 s, and a 407K-line TypeScript tree hits the 300 s module timeout with 840 MB RSS. The project fails its own gate (`./ubs . --ci` → 9 critical findings, all false positives of the Python constant-time-compare detector). Ten modules are copy-pasted siblings with drifted primitives, five documented meta-runner flags do not exist, inline suppression and severity normalisation are implemented in one module each, helper checksum mismatches fail open during scans, the installer aborts on a clean first install, the Claude Code save hook is never registered, and the docs (AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, modules/README.md, README) drift from the code.

## Goal
Deliver the README's promise for real: `ubs <file>` p95 < 1 s, a 50K-line polyglot repo < 10 s, a 400K-line TypeScript monorepo < 120 s, RSS < 200 MB, zero module timeouts on the benchmark corpus — and prove it continuously with a benchmark job whose regression alarm is statistically sound (CUSUM), not a brittle percentage.

## Measured baseline (this machine, 2026-09-02)
single Python file 5.8 s, single JS file 4.6 s; this repo (15 files) 9.1 s; test-suite tree (514 files, 29K lines, 10 languages) 40 s (~730 lines/s vs README's 10,000+); franchise_location_data_tool --only=python (597 files, 124K lines) 143 s; lumera_ai --only=js (407 files, 407K lines) module timeout at 300 s with 840 MB RSS; meta-runner overhead ≈ 1.7 s per invocation; JS module CPU/wall ≈ 0.18 → process-spawn bound. Profiling the JS module on 407 files: default 900 s+ (killed), without type narrowing 900 s+, without type narrowing and without category 7 (security/taint) 417 s → the taint/security category alone costs > 480 s and the remainder is still > 1 s per file.

## Mechanisms (each is its own bead)
1. Instrumentation (UBS_PROFILE=1) and a benchmark corpus + CI job with CUSUM alarms.
2. Necessary-literal prefilter: for every ast-grep rule and regex pattern extract the literal tokens any match must contain, run ONE ripgrep pass with the literal set to compute per-file rule bitsets, and run ast-grep / core analyzers only on files that can match.
3. Process budget ≤ 25 per module (delivered by epic A).
4. Meta-runner overhead ≤ 150 ms for single-file targets.
5. Merkle-keyed incremental cache: per-file findings keyed by content hash under H(engine‖module‖rulepack); per-directory Merkle nodes let whole unchanged subtrees be skipped.
6. LPT scheduler with a cost model (Graham's 4/3 bound) and work-stealing file shards inside a module.
7. Streaming everywhere (no slurping module output into shell variables).
8. Generated performance table in README; module timeout scaled by expected cost.


## Acceptance Criteria
All child beads closed with their acceptance tests green in CI; the epic's 'Done when' statement verified by a fresh scan and documented in CHANGELOG.

- Any change to modules/ubs-*.sh or modules/helpers/* must be followed by `./scripts/update_checksums.sh` and `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`; the CI drift check will flag modules against the last tag until the next release is cut (see the cut-release bead).
- Run `shellcheck -S warning` on touched shell files and `./ubs <touched files> --ci` before closing.

title: C1: UBS_PROFILE instrumentation, benchmark corpus, scripts/bench.sh and a CI bench job with CUSUM regression alarms
description:
## What
(1) `UBS_PROFILE=1` makes every module emit extras.profile {list_ms, prefilter_ms, ast_grep_ms, core_ms, render_ms, processes, files_considered, files_after_prefilter, categories:[{id,ms}]} and the meta-runner add list-build, copy, fan-out, merge timings. (3) CI job `bench` compares against benchmarks/baseline.json and, per corpus item, runs a two-sided CUSUM on log(wall) with drift k=0.5σ and threshold h=4σ (ARL₀≈500) so noisy runners do not produce flaky failures while a persistent 10% regression trips within a handful of runs. Bead C3's acceptance criterion (p95 overhead ≤ 150 ms) needs a measurement that survives load noise and is re-run on every bench job, not a one-off PS4 trace. Overhead (a difference of two means) is the right quantity because the module's own time swamps it.

title: C2: Necessary-literal prefilter — one ripgrep pass computes per-file rule bitsets; ast-grep and analyzers run only on files that can match
description:
## What
For every ast-grep rule (from the pack YAML: pattern literals, `kind`-independent identifiers, member names) and every regex-layer pattern, extract the set of literal tokens any match must contain (e.g. eval, innerHTML, .then(, compare_digest, ParseUnverified). Build one literal file per module and run ONE `rg --json -f literals.txt` (Aho–Corasick/regex-set inside ripgrep) over the file list to produce, per file, the bitset of rules whose literal set intersects it. Then invoke ast-grep `scan -c` only on the subset of files with any candidate rule (via --globs or a per-group file list) and pass the bitsets to ubs_core so analyzers skip files with no candidate. Rules with no extractable literal fall back to all files. Conservative by construction (a literal every match must contain), so results are identical; UBS_NO_PREFILTER=1 disables it for A/B.

title: C4: Merkle-keyed incremental cache — per-file findings replay, whole-subtree skip, atomic writes, hit-rate in profile
description:
## What
Cache root $XDG_CACHE_HOME/ubs/<H(engine‖module checksum‖rulepack hash)>/. Per-file entry keyed by BLAKE2b(file bytes) storing that file's NDJSON findings. Per-directory Merkle node = hash of child names+hashes (taken from `git ls-files -s` blob ids when in a clean git tree, else stat+content hash) so `ubs .` skips entire unchanged subtrees without re-hashing every file. Cross-file analyzers (D6) record their input set; a cached result is invalidated when any input changes. Writes are atomic (temp + rename), reads lock-free; --no-cache disables; profile reports hit-rate; `ubs doctor` reports cache size and offers `--prune-cache`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- test_cache.py: replay is byte-identical to a cold scan; second run on an unchanged corpus ≥ 5× faster; editing one file invalidates exactly that file's entry; rule-pack change invalidates everything; concurrent scans do not corrupt the cache.

## User-facing controls (added in refinement round 3)
`UBS_CACHE_DIR` overrides the cache root; `--no-cache` disables reads and writes; `--ci` keeps the cache enabled (keys include engine/module/rule-pack hashes so a stale cache cannot survive an upgrade) but `ubs doctor` reports cache size and age and offers `--prune-cache`; cache hits are visible in `extras.profile.cache_hit_rate` and in the text summary line so a suspicious result can be re-run with --no-cache.

title: C5: LPT scheduler with a fitted cost model and work-stealing file shards
description:
## What
Estimate per-module cost ĉ = a_lang · files_after_prefilter + b_lang with coefficients fitted from profiles (benchmarks/cost-model.json, refreshed by the nightly bench). title: C3b: One output pass per module run — fold inline suppressions, permalinks, metrics attach and the single-file path rewrite into a single python pass; skip .ubsignore parsing for explicit targets; lazy git metadata
description:
## What
After the single-file fast path (bead C3, 2026-09-03) the meta-runner's own cost on `ubs FILE --ci` is ~325–365 ms on top of the module (module 3.2–3.8 s for the Python fixture). The trace (PS4=$EPOCHREALTIME bash -x) attributes it to: apply_inline_suppressions ~75 ms (writes a temp python script, starts an interpreter; skipped since C3 when the single file has no marker), the text permalink python pass ~26 ms, attach_metrics_to_json ~23 ms, single_file_paths ~21 ms, the .ubsignore python parse ~20 ms, merge_json_scanners ~16 ms, and ~10 small spawns (date, mktemp, realpath, banner printf) ~30 ms. Fold the output-side passes into ONE python invocation per module run that takes the module's text/json/sarif outputs plus a small JSON of parameters (source root, workspace root, single-file target, git blob base, metrics dir) and performs all rewrites in memory; make the .ubsignore parse bash-only (or skip it when every target is an explicit file); resolve git metadata only when a permalink or report will actually be produced (text with a GitHub remote, json, sarif, html) — never for `--format=json` without a remote, never for `--list-categories`/`robot-docs`.

## Why
Bead C3's acceptance is p95 overhead ≤ 150 ms for single-file targets, because the agent hooks run `ubs FILE --ci` on every edit. The module dominates today, but the meta-runner's share is a fixed tax on every hook invocation across the swarm; the passes are all "read file, rewrite, write file" and belong in one process.

## How
1. New helper script embedded in `ubs` (heredoc into `$TMPDIR_RUN/postprocess.py` written once per run, not per module): functions strip_ansi, apply_suppressions (current semantics: markers ubs:ignore / ubs: disable / nolint / noqa on the finding line or the line above; keep the GH #91 caveats documented in A7), restore_paths (workspace → source; single-file basename → invocation-relative), add_permalinks (text and json/sarif; identical rules to add_json_permalinks/`repo_rel`), attach_metrics (current attach_metrics_to_json behaviour). One call per module output set; all files rewritten in place.
2. run_lang: replace the chain apply_inline_suppressions | restore_original_paths | attach_metrics_to_json | (text permalinks) with one call; keep the old functions only until B10 deletes the text-scraping fallbacks (they may still be used there).
3. .ubsignore: parse with bash `while read` (comments, blank lines, trailing-slash strip) — the file is tiny; or skip entirely when TARGETED_SCAN_MODE=1 and no directory targets (explicit files bypass ignores by design).
4. Lazy git: `resolve_git_metadata` becomes a memoised function called from the first consumer (permalink/report code); `ubs --format=json` still carries the git block (json is a consumer), text without a remote pays nothing.
5. Measure before/after with scripts/bench.sh single-file case (bead C3d) and with the PS4 trace; record numbers in the closing comment. Target: meta-minus-module ≤ 150 ms p95 on this box at load < 10, ≤ 250 ms under the usual load.
6. Contract checks: existing suppression, permalink, shareable and single-file checks must stay green (they are the regression net); add `single_file_one_postprocess_pass` asserting exactly one python spawn per module run via a `UBS_TRACE_SPAWNS=1` debug counter (cheap: increment a counter file in a wrapper function) — or, if that is more machinery than value, rely on the bench gate only and say so.

## Acceptance Criteria
- run_all green (except environment rust-clean); measured overhead recorded; bench single-file case shows the drop; README/robot-docs unchanged unless the env surface changes.

## Testing and logging requirements (apply to every bead)
- Unit tests live under test-suite/quality/ (Python, unittest, run by test-suite/run_all.sh) or test-suite/shareable/ for meta-runner behaviour; installer tests under test-suite/install/run_tests.sh. Every test prints a `[case-id] RUN/PASS/FAIL (elapsed)` line and, on failure, the full stdout/stderr it captured, so a swarm agent can diagnose from the log alone.
- E2E checks run the real `./ubs` (or the real module) against real fixture files with `--ci --format=json`, assert on exact rule ids / counts, and write artifacts under test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/.
- Any change to modules/ubs-*.sh, modules/helpers/* or modules/lib/* must be followed by `./scripts/update_checksums.sh` and `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`; any change to `ubs` or `install.sh` by `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`.
- Run `shellcheck -S warning` on touched shell files, `python3 scripts/check_docs_claims.py`, and `./ubs <touched files> --ci` before closing. Gates must run on a frozen tree with no other scans in flight (cargo's global lock and the module timeout checks are load-sensitive).
- Never close on a self-report: cite the gate output (run_all.sh, cli-contract, manifest case ids) in the closing comment, and name anything that could not be verified here (e.g. a CI job on a platform this box does not have).

title: C3c: Python and JS modules emit the per-finding JSON in the same pass as the summary (--report-json currently costs +0.8 s per run)
description:
## What
In json/jsonl/toon modes the meta-runner asks the python and js modules for `--report-json=FILE` (csharp: `--emit-findings-json`) in addition to `--format=json`. Measured on one Python file (2026-09-03): module alone 3.77 s, with `--report-json` 4.60 s — the module re-derives findings for the report instead of serialising what it already has. Make the findings JSON a by-product of the single analysis pass in ubs-python.sh and ubs-js.sh (and check csharp), so json mode costs the same as text mode.

## Why
Every `--format=json` scan (CI, agents, the dashboard paths) pays ~0.8 s per module per run for nothing; on the 447-case manifest that is minutes. The A4 ports (0xjg.4 python, 0xjg.5 js) will rewrite these modules onto ubs-common.sh/ubs_core — coordinate: if the port lands first, this bead is folded into it (state that in the closing comment); if this lands first, the port must keep the single-pass property (add it to the A4 acceptance).

## How
1. Locate where each module builds its text findings and where `--report-json` triggers a second walk/ast-grep run; capture finding records (rule id, file, line, severity, message, code sample) into an array during the main pass; write the report file at the end.
2. Verify with `UBS_PROFILE=1` + module timing: json mode ≈ text mode ± 5%.
3. Contract check: `report_json_no_extra_pass` — time-based checks are flaky; instead assert the module runs ast-grep once by counting `ast-grep`/`sg` invocations through a PATH shim that logs its argv (the test already has a shim pattern for cargo/npm) — count with and without --report-json must be equal.

title: Release self-scan gate is red: taint_py/sql_injection report incomplete analysis on this repo's own Python
description:
The release self-scan gate (`scripts/check_self_scan.py`, invoked by `scripts/cut-release.sh`) runs `./ubs . --ci --fail-on-warning --format=json` under `UBS_ALLOW_PARTIAL=0` and requires a fully complete scan: aggregate status `ok`, every language scanner `ok`, `failed_modules` empty, zero critical and zero warning. The gate has no opt-out.

Scanning this repository, the Python module exits 2 ("analysis incomplete"), so the gate rejects and no tagged release can be cut via `cut-release.sh`:

- `taint_py` raises `AnalysisLimit` ("Python taint analysis is incomplete") for roughly 110 components of this repo's own Python. Reasons, in `modules/helpers/ubs_core/analyzers/taint_py.py`:
  - "generator expression global writes require resume-state analysis" (:2137, :2180)
  - "dynamic globals mapping key" (:2992)
  - "generator with live lexical cells requires resume-state analysis" (:4473)
  - "generator global writes require resume-state analysis" (:4477)
  - "generator live global reads require resume-state analysis" (:4492)
  - "generator expression live delayed reads require resume-state analysis" (:5224)
- `sql_injection` raises `SQLFlowLimit` "SQL generator reducer callbacks are unresolved" in `modules/helpers/ubs_core/py_detectors/sql_injection.py` (:4001, :4792).

These refusal reasons are **absent at tag v5.5.26** (the last tag that passed this same strict self-scan) and **present on current main** — confirmed by comparing `modules/` at v5.5.26 against current. So the strict self-scan went red after v5.5.26: a gate regression caused by the taint engine becoming more conservative (adding fail-closed refusals) faster than the completeness work landed. These are deterministic modeling limits (generator / resume-state / dynamic-globals), not an environment or dependency problem.

Impact: `cut-release.sh` cannot cut a tagged release until the taint engine can model these constructs (resume-state / function-summary dataflow), or the gate's completeness policy changes for the project's own analyzer sources.

Depends on the taint-engine completeness work (monotone dataflow with function summaries).

title: Consider TOON variant for JSONL output
description: Investigate whether a TOON variant of JSONL output (--beads-jsonl) would be beneficial. Since JSONL is already compact (one record per line), TOON savings may be minimal. However, for large findings arrays within each JSONL record, tabular format could still help. Low priority - evaluate after primary TOON integration is complete.
close_reason: Decision: no TOON variant for JSONL. --beads-jsonl / --format=jsonl exist for line-delimited streaming into tools that read one JSON object per line (bd import, jq -c); TOON's savings come from tabular encoding of arrays across a whole document, which a per-line encoding cannot exploit, and a TOON line would no longer be JSONL for those consumers. Agents that want the compact form use --format=toon on the combined document, which now fails loudly when the encoder is missing (K5).

title: Epic G: Distribution channels — Docker runtime deps, Scoop, macOS and Windows CI
description:
## Background (reality check 2026-09-02, UBS v5.3.13)
The reality check compared README/AGENTS claims with the code and measured behaviour: 440/440 manifest cases pass, but single-file scans take 4.6–5.8 s (README says < 1 s), a 29K-line fixture tree takes 40 s (README: 3.2 s for 50K lines), a 124K-line Python project takes 143 s, and a 407K-line TypeScript tree hits the 300 s module timeout with 840 MB RSS. The project fails its own gate (`./ubs . --ci` → 9 critical findings, all false positives of the Python constant-time-compare detector). Ten modules are copy-pasted siblings with drifted primitives, five documented meta-runner flags do not exist, inline suppression and severity normalisation are implemented in one module each, helper checksum mismatches fail open during scans, the installer aborts on a clean first install, the Claude Code save hook is never registered, and the docs (AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, modules/README.md, README) drift from the code.

## Goal
Every install channel the README advertises is exercised by CI and actually works: the Docker image can run helpers and JS/TS scans (today it has no python3, unzip, or ast-grep, so helpers and JS/TS scans fail inside the container), Scoop is either real in this repo or removed from the README, macOS (bash 3.2 as /bin/bash) and Windows (Git Bash) get CI jobs, and Nix gets a run smoke.


## Acceptance Criteria
All child beads closed with their acceptance tests green in CI; the epic's 'Done when' statement verified by a fresh scan and documented in CHANGELOG.

## Testing and logging requirements (apply to every bead)
- Unit tests live under test-suite/quality/ (Python, unittest, run by test-suite/run_all.sh) or test-suite/shareable/ for meta-runner behaviour; installer tests under test-suite/install/run_tests.sh. Every test prints a `[case-id] RUN/PASS/FAIL (elapsed)` line and, on failure, the full stdout/stderr it captured, so a swarm agent can diagnose from the log alone.
- E2E scripts must run the real `./ubs` (or the real module) against real fixture files with `--ci --format=json`, assert on exact rule ids / counts, and write artifacts under test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/ (stdout.log, stderr.log, result.json).
- Any change to modules/ubs-*.sh or modules/helpers/* must be followed by `./scripts/update_checksums.sh` and `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`; the CI drift check will flag modules against the last tag until the next release is cut (see the cut-release bead).
- Run `shellcheck -S warning` on touched shell files and `./ubs <touched files> --ci` before closing.

## Success Criteria
Docker image scans JS and Python in CI; macOS and Windows jobs green; Scoop channel real or removed; Nix run smoke green.

title: G7: python3 resolution — accept `python` when it is Python 3 (Git Bash/Windows) through a per-run PATH shim; doctor names the interpreter
description:
## What
`ubs` and every module call `python3` by name (need_cmd python3, `python3 -`, helpers invoked as `python3 modules/helpers/x.py`). On Git for Windows there is usually no `python3` on PATH, only `python` (from python.org or uv), so helpers, the size guard's fallback, path restoration, inline suppressions and permalinks all silently degrade. Resolve once at start-up: if `python3` is missing but `python` (or `py -3`) reports Python ≥ 3.9, create `$TMPDIR_RUN/bin/python3` (a symlink on POSIX, a 2-line wrapper script on Windows) and prepend that directory to PATH for the whole run, so nothing else changes. `ubs doctor` prints "python: <path> (<version>)" or the reason it is unusable.

## Why
The windows-smoke job (bead G4) prints `python3: missing` diagnostics for exactly this reason; the README promises Windows via Git Bash. A shim is preferable to a `$PYTHON` variable because 10 modules and 14 helpers would otherwise need editing, and the modules must keep working when run directly.

## How
1. New function `resolve_python3` in `ubs` (near ensure_ast_grep): `command -v python3` → done; else try `python`, then `py -3`; verify with `"$cand" -c 'import sys; sys.exit(0 if sys.version_info >= (3, 9) else 1)'`; create the shim under `$TMPDIR_RUN/pybin/python3` (`ln -s` or `printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexec "%s" "$@"\n'`), `export PATH="$TMPDIR_RUN/pybin:$PATH"`. Must run after TMPDIR_RUN exists and before module fan-out and before any python3 use in the run (move the early `.ubsignore` python parse after it, or make that parse bash-only).
2. `UBS_PYTHON=/path` env override (documented in --help, robot-docs env, README env table) wins over detection.
3. `ubs doctor`: "python: ready <path> <version>" / info "python: not found (helpers, permalinks and suppressions degrade; set UBS_PYTHON)".
4. Contract check `python_shim_when_only_python_exists`: PATH shim dir where `python3` is absent and `python` is a symlink to the real interpreter; run a python fixture scan; assert helper-backed findings (e.g. resource_lifecycle_py) are present and doctor reports the shim path.
5. windows-smoke job: drop the "python3 missing" diagnostic line once doctor reports it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Contract check green on Linux; `ubs doctor` shows the interpreter; windows-smoke shows helper findings on the Python smoke scan after the job has been observed (bead G6).

## Testing and logging requirements (apply to every bead)
- Unit tests live under test-suite/quality/ (Python, unittest, run by test-suite/run_all.sh) or test-suite/shareable/ for meta-runner behaviour; installer tests under test-suite/install/run_tests.sh. Every test prints a `[case-id] RUN/PASS/FAIL (elapsed)` line and, on failure, the full stdout/stderr it captured, so a swarm agent can diagnose from the log alone.
- E2E checks run the real `./ubs` (or the real module) against real fixture files with `--ci --format=json`, assert on exact rule ids / counts, and write artifacts under test-suite/artifacts/<case-id>/.
- Any change to modules/ubs-*.sh, modules/helpers/* or modules/lib/* must be followed by `./scripts/update_checksums.sh` and `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`; any change to `ubs` or `install.sh` by `./scripts/update_sha256sums.sh`.
- Run `shellcheck -S warning` on touched shell files, `python3 scripts/check_docs_claims.py`, and `./ubs <touched files> --ci` before closing. Gates must run on a frozen tree with no other scans in flight (cargo's global lock and the module timeout checks are load-sensitive).
- Never close on a self-report: cite the gate output (run_all.sh, cli-contract, manifest case ids) in the closing comment, and name anything that could not be verified here (e.g. a CI job on a platform this box does not have).
notes: 2026-10-09 G7 correctness follow-up: freeze an absolute executable before adding the per-run python3 wrapper, preserving the final virtualenv symlink; validate python3 as well as fallback python and py -3. The prior named UBS_PYTHON=python3 path recursively re-entered its wrapper and timed out before module execution; invalid/crashing python3 candidates also prevented usable fallback. Independent baseline: 17 resolver controls yielded 5 passes, 11 assertion failures and 1 timeout. Frozen candidate: all 17 controls and 36 actual public CLI calls pass on CPython 3.14.8 with ast-grep 0.45.3, including named/relative overrides, relative PATH/empty components, changed cwd, spaces/metacharacters, CDPATH, virtualenv identity, rejected/missing interpreter fallback, preserved py -3 argv, doctor output, clean/unsafe scans and Python/JS/Rust JSON/SARIF/error envelopes. The 22-method independent run completed in 235.603s; receipt test-suite/artifacts/python-resolution-checkpoint/independent-receipt.json and independent-public.log. No Windows or actual Python 3.9 runtime claim. Existing closure and historical comments preserved.

title: Kotlin lazy and block initializers that build requests from fields scan as plain initializers
description:
The Java/Kotlin SSRF check treats a class field initializer as deferred executable code, and reports incomplete analysis, only when the initializer contains `->`, `new T(...) {` or `object :` (the v5.5.26 fix for #194). A Kotlin block or delegate initializer has none of these: `val later = lazy { RequestEntity.get(u!!).build() }`, `val c by lazy { ... }`, `val f = { ... }`. It is read as an ordinary initializer that runs at construction. If the block builds a request from a field that a request handler sets later, the scan says ok instead of incomplete. v5.5.13 and v5.5.3 report ok here too.

Matching every `= {` and `by lazy {` block closes the gap but makes ordinary code partial: `val client by lazy { OkHttpClient.Builder().build() }` would end exit 2, which is the complaint in #194. That variant was measured in the v5.5.26 review and not shipped.

Follow-up: treat a Kotlin deferred block as executable class initialization only when a `.build(` chain in it starts from a request type (`RequestEntity`, `Request.Builder`, `HttpRequest.newBuilder`, `WebClient`, and so on), so client builders stay ok.

Done when, with the review's probe rows, f (`val later = lazy { RequestEntity.get(u!!).build() }` with a parameter read) scans partial, g (`val client by lazy { OkHttpClient.Builder().build() }` with a header read) scans ok, rows a to e are unchanged, and the JWT verification and security_precision test modules pass.

title: ubs doctor: verify ast-grep availability (and fix if tool cache exists)
description: Add explicit ast-grep diagnostics to 'ubs doctor' so users can quickly understand whether JS/TS scanning will be accurate. Optionally support --fix to download ast-grep into the tool cache when missing.

title: ubs: standardize exit code 2 as 'environment error' and surface it nicely
description: If language modules adopt exit code 2 for dependency/environment failures (e.g., JS module refusing TSX fallback without ast-grep), the ubs meta-runner should recognize and report it distinctly from 'findings' failures.

title: Type narrowing heuristics fallback

notes: Fallback heuristics implemented inside type_narrowing_ts.js (text-based scan when TypeScript module missing) and integrated into ubs-js run_type_narrowing_checks.
